## Typography

_Source: `apps/storybook/src/foundations/typography.mdx`_

# Typography

**Related:** [Tokens catalog](/?path=/docs/foundations-tokens--docs) · [Minimum-class defaults](/?path=/docs/foundations-minimum-class-defaults--docs) · [Typography sample](/?path=/docs/core-molecules-typography-sample--docs) · [Prose](/?path=/docs/core-molecules-prose--docs) · [Flow](/?path=/docs/core-molecules-flow--docs) · [Heading](/?path=/docs/core-atoms-heading--docs) · [Paragraph](/?path=/docs/core-atoms-paragraph--docs) · [List](/?path=/docs/core-molecules-list--docs) · [Caption](/?path=/docs/core-atoms-caption--docs)

Type roles and usage for UI. Live size specimens also appear under [Foundations → Tokens → Typography](/?path=/docs/foundations-tokens--docs). Color architecture is separate: [Color Tokens](/?path=/docs/foundations-color-tokens-architecture--docs).

Typography in Eevenkoto follows the same tier discipline as color: raw optical values live in Tier 1; roles that UI consumes live in Tier 2; component bridges live in Tier 3.

```
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Tier 1: Type scale (primitive-tokens.css)               │
│  --eevenkoto-font-size-sm … 3xl, font-weight-*         │
└──────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────┘
                           │ Mapped to roles
                           ▼
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Tier 2: Semantic type (tokens.css)                    │
│  heading-*, body-*, caption, control-*                 │
└──────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────┘
                           │ Consumed by primitives / components
                           ▼
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Tier 3: Heading, Paragraph, List, Caption, Button, …  │
│  Private bridges + public override APIs                │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Families

| Token | Face | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--eevenkoto-font-sans` | Inter | Body, UI controls, meso/micro headings |
| `--eevenkoto-font-serif` | Outfit | Macro + H3 display headings |

## Heading hierarchy (multi-axis)

Six levels are grouped into three visual tiers. **Do not rely on size alone** — micro levels match body size and differentiate via case, posture, and placement.

| Visual tier | Levels | Primary tools |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Macro** | H1, H2 | Size jump, bottom rule, generous space-before |
| **Meso** | H3, H4 | Modest size + weight; H4 near body; no tint bands |
| **Micro** | H5, H6 | Same size as `body-md`; small caps (H5); bold italic / run-in (H6) |

Details and examples live on [Heading](/?path=/docs/core-atoms-heading--docs).

## Font sizes — two tiers

### Tier 1 (scale)

Sparse rem steps in `primitive-tokens.css`: `sm` → `3xl`. These answer “how large is this optical step?” **Never reference Tier 1 sizes from component stylesheets.**

### Tier 2 (semantic)

Role aliases in `tokens.css`. Grammar: `--eevenkoto-font-size-[role]-[variant]`.

| Role | Tokens | Typical consumer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `heading` | `heading-1` … `heading-6` | Heading primitive (`4`/`5` → lg; `6` → body-md) |
| `body` | `body-sm`, `body-md`, `body-lg` | Paragraph, List, document `body` |
| `caption` | `caption` | Caption primitive |
| `control` | `control-sm`, `control-md`, `control-lg` | Button, Badge, Chip |

### Component size props (`sm | md | lg`)

Public size props across Button, Paragraph, List, and Badge use the same **`sm | md | lg`** names. Do not reintroduce `small` / `large`. Host CSS may omit `--md` (the base class is already md); framework helpers still emit an explicit `--md` when assembling class strings so the prop API stays aligned across controls.

| Prop value | Typical Tier 2 font role |
| --- | --- |
| `sm` | `control-sm` or `body-sm` |
| `md` | `control-md` or `body-md` (default) |
| `lg` | `control-lg` or `body-lg` |

Themes or density modes can remap a role without renaming the rem ladder.

```css
/* Correct: semantic intent */
.eevenkoto-button {
  font-size: var(--eevenkoto-font-size-control-md);
}

/* Incorrect: Tier 1 scale in a component */
.eevenkoto-button {
  font-size: var(--eevenkoto-font-size-md);
}
```

## Weights

Tier 1 weights (loaded with the faces):

| Token | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `--eevenkoto-font-weight-regular` | `400` |
| `--eevenkoto-font-weight-semibold` | `600` |
| `--eevenkoto-font-weight-bold` | `700` |

Italic bold is loaded for Inter so H6 can use bold italic posture.

## Line heights

| Token | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `--eevenkoto-line-height-tight` | Macro/meso headings, controls |
| `--eevenkoto-line-height-body` | Paragraphs, captions, H4–H6, page body |

## Content color

Pair type with `--eevenkoto-color-content-primary`, `--eevenkoto-color-content-secondary`, `--eevenkoto-color-content-tertiary`, or `--eevenkoto-color-content-disabled` — never hue primitives.

| Role | Token | Typical component |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Body / titles | `content-primary` | Paragraph (default), Heading |
| De-emphasized body | `content-secondary` | Paragraph `--secondary` |
| Metadata / helpers | `content-tertiary` | Caption (default), Field hint |

## Caption vs Paragraph

| Need | Use |
| --- | --- |
| Multi-sentence body or supporting prose | **[Paragraph](/?path=/docs/core-atoms-paragraph--docs)** |
| One-line metadata, timestamp, or field helper | **[Caption](/?path=/docs/core-atoms-caption--docs)** |
| De-emphasize a full paragraph without making it metadata | Paragraph `tone="secondary"` |
| Quiet ink for Caption | Default (maps to `content-tertiary`) — not Paragraph secondary |

## Usage rules

- Prefer **Heading** for section structure; do not fake titles with bold Paragraph.
- Use **one `h1` per view**; do not skip levels only for visual size.
- Differentiate **H5/H6 with posture and case**, not a size below body.
- Limit structural rules/tints to **macro** headings (H1/H2).
- Use **Caption** for metadata and helper copy — not for main body text.
- Do not use **Paragraph `sm` + secondary** as a Caption substitute — size and ink roles differ.
- Button label size comes from **`control-*`**, not `body-*`.

See the [Tokens → Typography](/?path=/docs/foundations-tokens--docs) story for live specimens.

# Authoring foundations

For day-to-day contributor rules see `/AGENTS.md` (or repo-root `AGENTS.md`). Deep color architecture follows.

## Color architecture

_Source: `apps/storybook/src/foundations/color-tokens-architecture.mdx`_

# Color Token Architecture

**Audience:** authors extending the system — not the app usage guide. For “what tokens exist to consume,” see [Foundations → Tokens](/?path=/docs/foundations-tokens--docs). For install/use feed-in, see repo `llms.txt` / `llms-full.txt`.

**Doc set:** Architecture (this file) → [Tier 1 Primitives](./color-tokens-tier1-primitives.mdx) → [Tier 2 Semantics](./color-tokens-tier2-semantics.mdx) → [Tier 3 Component Scoping](./color-tokens-tier3-component-scoping.mdx)

This document defines the architectural rationale, color-space mechanics, theming model, accessibility guardrails, and governance flowchart for the Eevenkoto color token system. Tier-specific naming, invariants, and examples live in the linked docs above.

## Core Architectural Philosophy

Traditional design systems frequently adopt numerical ramps for primitive palettes (e.g., `--color-blue-50` through `--color-blue-900`). While systematic, this pattern creates three foundational failures:

1. **Illusion of Completeness:** Teams spend hours calibrating steps (100, 200, …, 900) that are never rendered in the interface.

2. **Ambiguous Utility:** An engineer or designer choosing between `blue-500` and `blue-600` is forced to make an aesthetic guess rather than an intentional ergonomic choice.

3. **Decoupled Hue Behavior:** Colors do not behave identically across lightness scales. A yellow at lightness L = 0.85 functions as a vibrant background; a blue at L = 0.85 is often an anemic, illegible wash.

The Eevenkoto system departs from numerical ramps by implementing a **function-first primitive model** inspired by the functional mapping of Radix Colors, coupled with an absolute three-tier separation of concerns.

```
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Tier 1: Primitives (primitive-tokens.css)               │
│  Function-first pigment library in isolated color space│
└──────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────┘
                           │ Mapped per theme (Light / Dark / Contrast)
                           ▼
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Tier 2: Semantics (tokens.css)                        │
│  System-wide intent, UX roles, and contextual meaning  │
└──────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────┘
                           │ Consumed as fallback defaults
                           ▼
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Tier 3: Component Scoping (*.css)                     │
│  Element boundaries, private bridges, and local APIs   │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

| Tier | Source file | Responsibility | Consumers |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 — Primitives | `packages/css/tokens/primitive-tokens.css` | Sparse OKLCH pigment library | Tier 2 only |
| 2 — Semantics | `packages/css/tokens/tokens.css` | Intent, theming, contrast pairs | Layouts, utilities, Tier 3 |
| 3 — Components | `packages/css/core/...` or `domain/...` | Private bridges + public override API | Host component only |

## Color Space Mechanics: OKLCH & Display P3

All color definitions across the system are authored natively in **OKLCH** (`oklch(L C H [/ A])`).

```
Color specification: oklch(Lightness [0–1], Chroma [0–0.4], Hue [0–360] [/ Alpha])
```

### Why OKLCH?

- **Perceptual Uniformity:** In standard sRGB and HSL, hue and lightness are entangled. For example, pure sRGB yellow (`hsl(60, 100%, 50%)`) has a perceived lightness drastically higher than pure sRGB blue (`hsl(240, 100%, 50%)`). In OKLCH, two colors with L = 0.60 share identical perceived luminance, allowing predictable contrast calculations across disparate hues.

- **Independent Chroma Control:** Chroma (C) can be adjusted to desaturate or supercharge a hue without altering its lightness or disrupting accessibility deltas.

- **P3 Gamut Access:** Modern mobile and desktop displays reproduce colors far outside standard sRGB. OKLCH unlocks the wider Display P3 color space natively without clipping.

### Color-Mix & Interpolation

Interactive transitions and subtle tints leverage `color-mix(in display-p3, ...)` to ensure that gradients and transitions do not pass through muddy, desaturated gray zones during interpolation.

At **Tier 2**, prefer direct aliases to Tier 1 primitives for brand and chrome. Reserve `color-mix` for documented recipes (transparent fades, disabled endpoints) — do not invent muted brand hues by blending two pigments. See [Tier 1 — Prefer a new primitive](./color-tokens-tier1-primitives.mdx) and [Tier 2 — Prefer aliases](./color-tokens-tier2-semantics.mdx).

## Environmental Adaptations & Theming

### Light vs. Dark Elevation Models

Dark mode is fundamentally different from inverting lightness (L<sub>dark</sub> ≠ 1 − L<sub>light</sub>).

- **Light Mode (Subtractive & Atmospheric):**
  - Canvas is light parchment (`oklch(0.96 0.02 90)`).
  - Elevation and separation are communicated through **ambient shadows**, subtle border lines, and parchment tone variations.

- **Dark Mode (Additive & Luminous):**
  - Canvas is deep charcoal/obsidian (`oklch(0.14 0.01 240)`).
  - Shadows disappear into dark backgrounds. Elevation is communicated by **stepping lightness upward**:
    - Canvas root: L = 0.14
    - Surface Layer 1 (Cards, Sidebars): L = 0.18
    - Surface Layer 2 (Modals, Popovers): L = 0.23

- **The Chroma Vibration Guardrail:** High-chroma colors on pitch-dark surfaces cause visual vibration (halation). In dark mode, state and action tokens must be remapped to variants with **slightly decreased chroma (C)** and elevated lightness (L) to maintain legibility without fatiguing the eye.

Theme remapping happens **only at Tier 2**. See [Tier 2 Semantics](./color-tokens-tier2-semantics.mdx).

### High Contrast & Forced Colors Mode

When operating under assistive settings (e.g. Windows High Contrast Mode or `@media (forced-colors: active)`):

- System colors override author CSS colors (`Canvas`, `CanvasText`, `Highlight`, `ButtonText`).
- Gradients and subtle box-shadows disappear entirely.
- **Architecture Rule:** Every interactive component must define an explicit `border` (even if set to `transparent` in standard mode). In forced-colors mode, transparent borders are automatically converted into visible system outlines, preserving component hit-boxes and structural hierarchy.

## Accessibility in Practice vs. Theory

Theoretical contrast formulas (such as simple WCAG 2.1 math) often fail in real-world rendering engines, particularly when dealing with complex gradients or chromatic backgrounds.

### Practical Validation Guardrails

1. **Spatial Frequency Check**

   Contrast is perceived differently across shapes:

   - Body text (16px) requires higher lightness deltas (ΔL ≥ 0.50) against its background.
   - Bold interactive outlines or large buttons remain legible at lower deltas (ΔL ≥ 0.30).
   - Thin icons (1px strokes) must use high-impact tokens rather than muted border tokens to remain distinct.

2. **Focus Ring Luminance Guarantee**

   A focus ring must stand out equally against both the component's inner fill and the parent page canvas.

   - A single pale gold ring (`oklch(0.92 0.22 75)`) on parchment (`oklch(0.96 0.02 90)`) fails WCAG non-text contrast because the two lightness levels are nearly indistinguishable.
   - Focus rings must use a high-contrast delta (e.g., deep gold/amber `oklch(0.65 0.20 65)` or an offset compound outline) to guarantee immediate visibility regardless of placement.

## Governance & Token Decision Flowchart

When an engineer or designer needs a new style, follow this process before writing CSS:

```
                  Need a color for a UI element
                                │
                                ▼
                 Does a Tier 2 token express this
                 intent? (e.g. --color-control-*, --color-surface-*)
                                │
               ┌────────────────┴────────────────┐
              YES                                NO
               │                                 │
               ▼                                 ▼
   Consume Tier 2 in component       Does this represent a new,
   bridge (--_component-prop)        reusable system intent?
                                                 │
                                 ┌───────────────┴───────────────┐
                                YES                              NO
                                 │                               │
                                 ▼                               ▼
                 Check Tier 1 Primitives           Do not create a token.
                 Does the hue/function exist?      Use a local contextual
                                 │                 override via component API.
                 ┌───────────────┴───────────────┐
                YES                              NO
                 │                               │
                 ▼                               ▼
      Map Tier 1 to a new              [HUMAN FRICTION CHECKPOINT]
      Tier 2 semantic token            Collaborate with designer to
                                       author a new functional primitive
                                       in primitive-tokens.css
```
## Tier 1 — Primitives

_Source: `apps/storybook/src/foundations/color-tokens-tier1-primitives.mdx`_

# Tier 1: Primitives

**Audience:** authors extending pigments — not app usage. Consumable tokens: [Foundations → Tokens](/?path=/docs/foundations-tokens--docs).

**Doc set:** [Architecture](./color-tokens-architecture.mdx) → Tier 1 Primitives (this file) → [Tier 2 Semantics](./color-tokens-tier2-semantics.mdx) → [Tier 3 Component Scoping](./color-tokens-tier3-component-scoping.mdx)

Tier 1 is the sparse, hand-tuned pigment library. It holds raw OKLCH coordinates and grows only through an accretive, designer-reviewed process.

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Source file | `packages/css/tokens/primitive-tokens.css` |
| Naming convention | `--eevenkoto-color-<colorname>-<function>[-<variant>]` |
| Consumer scope | **Tier 2 only.** Never reference Tier 1 primitives directly in component stylesheets. |

## The Primitive Thought Experiment

Primitives do not describe how a color is deployed across the entire application. Instead, they answer a targeted question:

> *"If an entire monochrome interface were sculpted exclusively out of this single hue, what functional role would this specific shade perform?"*

Because colors are defined by functional affordances rather than arbitrary integers, primitive values reflect deliberate design interventions. A subtle tint might shift hue slightly toward green or violet to keep the atmosphere organic, rather than relying on a purely mathematical reduction of chroma.

## The Canonical Functional Scale

Primitives are authored strictly within this functional taxonomy:

| Function Role | Description | Common Variants |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `background` | Broad structural canvases (page root, large panes). | `background-subtle`, `background-element` |
| `state` | Interactive mechanics and active states. | `state-hover`, `state-active` |
| `border` | Boundary definitions, separators, and outlines. | `border-subtle` |
| `primary` | High-impact, punchy focal points, icons, and hero elements. | `primary-hover`, `primary-strong` |
| `text` | Readable content calibrated for typography. | `text-muted`, `text-shadow` |
| `tint` | Atmospheric washes and disabled mix partners (C=0 endpoints). | `tint-cool`, `tint-deep`, `tint-disabled`, `tint-disabled-deep` |
| `shadow` | Hue-tinted elevation / brand shadow pigments (composed at Tier 2). | — |

```css
/* Example: Primitives for Turquoise & Parchment */
:root {
  /* Turquoise */
  --eevenkoto-color-turquoise-state:          oklch(0.50 0.28 180);
  --eevenkoto-color-turquoise-state-hover:    oklch(0.30 0.22 170);
  --eevenkoto-color-turquoise-border-subtle:  oklch(0.10 0.22 180 / 20%);
  --eevenkoto-color-turquoise-primary:        oklch(0.85 0.24 165);
  --eevenkoto-color-turquoise-primary-hover:  oklch(0.70 0.28 180);
  --eevenkoto-color-turquoise-text:           oklch(0.98 0.01 190);
  --eevenkoto-color-turquoise-tint-cool:      oklch(0.98 0.015 202);
  --eevenkoto-color-turquoise-tint-deep:      oklch(0.18 0.22 162);
  /* Disabled mix partners: mode endpoints (C=0, A=0). Tier 2 picks light vs deep. */
  --eevenkoto-color-turquoise-tint-disabled:      oklch(1 0 180 / 0%);
  --eevenkoto-color-turquoise-tint-disabled-deep: oklch(0 0 180 / 0%);
  --eevenkoto-color-turquoise-shadow:         oklch(0.15 0.25 192 / 25%);
  --eevenkoto-color-turquoise-text-shadow:    oklch(0.12 0.20 192);

  /* Parchment */
  --eevenkoto-color-parchment-background:         oklch(0.96 0.02 90);
  --eevenkoto-color-parchment-background-subtle:  oklch(0.97 0.014 90);
  --eevenkoto-color-parchment-background-element: oklch(0.90 0.04 85);
  --eevenkoto-color-parchment-border:             oklch(0.50 0.18 80);
  --eevenkoto-color-parchment-primary:            oklch(0.40 0.10 80);
  --eevenkoto-color-parchment-text:               oklch(0.18 0.02 85);
  --eevenkoto-color-parchment-text-muted:         oklch(0.35 0.04 85);
  --eevenkoto-color-parchment-tint-disabled:      oklch(1 0 85 / 0%);
  --eevenkoto-color-parchment-tint-disabled-deep: oklch(0 0 85 / 0%);
}
```

See [Foundations → Tokens](/?path=/docs/foundations-tokens--docs) for the live swatch list of every primitive currently in CSS.

## Sparse Primitives vs. Completism

**Never create a Tier 1 token for the sake of completism.**

Do not generate empty scales or preemptive tokens. Authoring arbitrary 10-step ramps (50–900) creates gamut clipping and unused mid-tones. Primitives are added only when an interface requirement demands a new optical benchmark.

If an engineer needs a color that does not exist in Tier 1, this friction is an intentional system checkpoint. The new primitive must be created in direct collaboration with a designer to verify:

1. Whether an existing functional primitive already satisfies the need.
2. Whether the requested shade maintains harmony across both light and dark themes.

### Prefer a new primitive over a “muted mix”

When UI chrome needs a quieter accent (for example ability labels vs proficient-save gold), **do not invent that shade by `color-mix`-ing two Tier 1 hues in Tier 2**. Mixing pigments to fake a missing stop looks fine until a designer retunes Tier 1 — then every mix shifts in unpredictable, often muddy ways.

| Need | Do | Don’t |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Quiet parchment chrome | Alias `parchment-primary` / `parchment-border` at Tier 2 | `color-mix(gold, parchment-border)` |
| Bright emphasis | Alias `gold-primary-strong` (or add a reviewed gold stop) | Mix gold with text/border to “tone it down” |
| Deep chrome on sunken | Alias `gold-primary-deep` (≥3:1 vs sunken) | Reuse a light gold that fails non-text contrast |
| Truly new optical stop | Add a Tier 1 primitive with a designer | Encode the pigment only as a Tier 2 mix |

Friction to add a primitive is intentional: it keeps Tier 1 the single place pigments are authored.

## Consumption Rules

- Tier 2 maps primitives to semantic intent (see [Tier 2 Semantics](./color-tokens-tier2-semantics.mdx)).
- Components must never import or reference `--eevenkoto-color-<hue>-*` primitives directly (see [Tier 3 Component Scoping](./color-tokens-tier3-component-scoping.mdx)).
- Tier 1 values remain stable libraries of available pigments; themes do not rewrite primitive definitions.
## Tier 2 — Semantics

_Source: `apps/storybook/src/foundations/color-tokens-tier2-semantics.mdx`_

# Tier 2: Semantic Token Architecture

**Audience:** authors mapping intent — not the app usage catalog. For tokens that exist today, see [Foundations → Tokens](/?path=/docs/foundations-tokens--docs).

**Doc set:** [Architecture](./color-tokens-architecture.mdx) → [Tier 1 Primitives](./color-tokens-tier1-primitives.mdx) → Tier 2 Semantics (this file) → [Tier 3 Component Scoping](./color-tokens-tier3-component-scoping.mdx)

This document defines the naming grammar, architectural invariants, and governance rules for the semantic token layer (Tier 2). Tier 2 translates Tier 1 primitive pigments into web platform tokens (background, text, border, outline) and enforces color contrast and pairing guarantees.

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Source file | `packages/css/tokens/tokens.css` |
| Naming convention | `--eevenkoto-color-[domain]-[variant]-[element]-[state]` |
| Consumer scope | Global layouts, utilities, and Tier 3 component definitions |

## Architecture & Scope

The Eevenkoto token system uses a strict three-tier hierarchy:

- **Tier 1: Primitives** (`primitive-tokens.css`) — A sparse palette of hand-tuned OKLCH pigment curves. Tier 1 is the sole repository of raw color coordinates (`oklch()`, Display P3) and grows strictly through an accretive, append-only process.
- **Tier 2: Semantics** (`tokens.css`) — The complete semantic dictionary for the web platform. Tier 2 contains zero raw color values; every token maps Tier 1 primitives to functional UI roles. Color contrast, container pairing, and theme remapping are enforced here.
- **Tier 3: Components** (`*.css`) — Component-scoped styles. Components consume Tier 2 tokens through private `--_*` bridge variables. Component stylesheets are strictly isolated from Tier 1.

### The Golden Rule of Consumption

1. **Tier 2 consumes Tier 1.** Tier 2 references primitive variables directly.
2. **Tier 3 consumes Tier 2.** Components reference `--eevenkoto-color-*` tokens.
3. **Components never consume Tier 1.** Direct primitive references in component stylesheets break encapsulation and fail CI builds.

### Sparse Primitives vs. Vast Semantics

- **Tier 1 must remain sparse:** Authoring arbitrary 10-step ramps (50–900) creates gamut clipping and unused mid-tones. Primitives are added only when an interface requirement demands a new optical benchmark.
- **Tier 2 must be vast:** User interfaces require distinct tokens for states, surfaces, forms, and feedback. If Tier 2 is incomplete, engineers are forced to make aesthetic guesses or repurpose unrelated tokens. Tier 2 provides an exhaustive, predictable vocabulary for the entire platform.

## Naming Grammar & Domain Matrix

Tier 2 tokens use standard web platform terminology (background, text, border, outline) rather than physical pigment names.

Tokens follow a four-part grammar:

```text
--eevenkoto-color-[domain]-[variant]-[element]-[state]
```

Examples:

```text
--eevenkoto-color-   [domain]   -   [variant]   -   [element]      -   [state]
                      surface        canvas          (background)       default
                      surface        raised          border             default
                      content        primary         (text)             default
                      link           default         text               hover
                      control        primary         background         active
                      control        primary         text               disabled
                      form           input           border             invalid
                      feedback       caution         text               default
                      boundary       focus-outer     outline            default
                      depth          shadow          umbra              default
```

### The 8 Functional Domains

| Domain | Description | Elements | Supported States |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `surface` | Spatial layers, canvas backplates, cards, modals, wells | background, border | default |
| `content` | Body prose, headings, captions, icons; quiet chrome (`accent`) vs emphasis (`accent-strong`) | text, icon | default, hover (interactive wrappers) |
| `link` | Inline text navigation, breadcrumbs, action text | text, underline | default, hover, active, visited, focus |
| `control` | Contained interactive elements (buttons, chips, pills) | background, text, border, icon | default, hover, active, disabled, focus |
| `form` | Inputs, checkboxes, radios, switch tracks, thumbs | background, text, placeholder, border, message | default, hover, focus, checked, disabled, invalid |
| `feedback` | Standalone status messaging (banners, toasts, badges) | background, text, border, icon | default |
| `boundary` | Structural dividers and dual-halo focus indicators | border, outline | default |
| `depth` | Elevation shadows and ambient occlusion | umbra, penumbra, ambient | default |

### Domain Boundaries & Aliasing

#### Control vs. Feedback

- `feedback` owns contextual status palettes across **subtle** (default) and **solid** modes, plus outline surfaces derived in Tier 3 from the subtle tuple.
- Authored intents: `neutral`, `info`, `success`, `caution`, `critical`, `admin`.
- Hue map (Tier 1 → intent): parchment→neutral, turquoise→info, green→success, orange→caution, crimson→critical, purple→admin. New hues may be **placeholders** until a designer finalizes them.
- **Subtle fills are authored in Tier 2 with `color-mix(in oklch, var(--eevenkoto-color-*-state) …%, transparent)`** — never raw `oklch` inside component CSS (Badge, future banners/toasts).
- `control` maintains the vocabulary for buttons and future chips/pills. High-urgency actions consume `--eevenkoto-color-control-destructive-*` (aliases to the critical/crimson trajectory when authored). Button authors always consume the `control` domain.
- Badge (status) → `feedback` only. Chip (interactive filter) → `control`. StatusDot → `feedback` solid fills, unlabeled.

#### Form Validation vs. Feedback

- `feedback` is reserved for standalone messaging containers (alert banners, toasts, status chips).
- `form` maintains dedicated semantic validation tuples:

```css
--eevenkoto-color-form-input-background-invalid: ...;
--eevenkoto-color-form-input-text-invalid:       ...;
--eevenkoto-color-form-input-border-invalid:     ...;
--eevenkoto-color-form-input-message-invalid:    ...;
```

Form components consume only the `form` domain.

## Core Architectural Invariants

### 3.1 Zero Raw Literals

**Rule:** Tier 2 tokens must never contain raw color values (`hex`, `rgb()`, `hsl()`, `oklch()`).

**Allowed values:**

- `var(--eevenkoto-color-*)` primitive references (**preferred** for brand, chrome, and content accents)
- `color-mix(in oklch, ...)` operating purely on primitive variables — **only** for the documented recipes below
- Platform keywords: `transparent` and `currentColor`
- CSS system color keywords for Windows High Contrast Mode (`Canvas`, `CanvasText`, `ButtonBorder`, `Highlight`, `HighlightText`, `LinkText`)

**Planned enforcement:** Stylelint should fail CI if raw color strings appear in `tokens.css` (not wired yet). If an intent requires an unvetted color stop, it must be added to Tier 1 via the primitive review process.

### 3.1a Prefer aliases — constrain `color-mix`

Tier 2’s job is to **name intent**, not to invent pigments. Prefer a direct alias to an existing Tier 1 stop.

`color-mix` at Tier 2 is easy to overuse. Blending two chromatic primitives (for example gold × parchment-border) to fake a “muted accent” looks fine until Tier 1 is retuned — then every dependent mix drifts, often into muddy or oversaturated results that no one authored.

| Allowed mix recipes | Examples |
| --- | --- |
| Fade a primitive toward `transparent` | `boundary-subtle`, feedback subtle fills, link underlines, depth umbra/penumbra |
| Mix with mode endpoints (`*-tint-disabled` / `*-tint-disabled-deep`) | Disabled control / content tuples |

| Disallowed without a new Tier 1 stop | Why |
| --- | --- |
| Hue × hue “muted brand” mixes | Unstable when either primitive changes; hides a missing pigment |
| Mixes that exist only to avoid adding a primitive | Friction is intentional — see [Tier 1 — Prefer a new primitive](/?path=/docs/foundations-color-tokens-tier-1-primitives--docs) |

```css
/* ✅ Quiet chrome: alias parchment */
--eevenkoto-color-content-accent: var(--eevenkoto-color-parchment-primary);
--eevenkoto-color-content-accent-strong: var(--eevenkoto-color-gold-primary-deep);

/* ✅ Documented fade */
--eevenkoto-color-boundary-subtle: color-mix(
  in oklch,
  var(--eevenkoto-color-parchment-border) 35%,
  transparent
);

/* ❌ Don’t invent muted gold by mixing pigments */
/* --eevenkoto-color-content-accent: color-mix(in oklch, var(--gold-primary) 45%, var(--parchment-border) 55%); */
```

### 3.2 Coupled Background-Text Tuples & Opaque Disabled States

**Rule:** A background token must never be declared or remapped in isolation. Every container background belongs to an explicit tuple:

```css
--eevenkoto-color-[domain]-[variant]-background:  /* Container fill */
--eevenkoto-color-[domain]-[variant]-text:        /* Primary text (>= 4.5:1) */
--eevenkoto-color-[domain]-[variant]-text-subtle: /* Secondary text (>= 3.0:1) */
--eevenkoto-color-[domain]-[variant]-border:      /* Boundary stroke */
```

**Ban on Opacity for Disabled States:** Setting `opacity: 0.5` causes canvas bleed-through and unpredictable contrast failures. Disabled states must define explicit, opaque tokens:

```css
--eevenkoto-color-control-[variant]-background-disabled: /* Opaque fill */
--eevenkoto-color-control-[variant]-text-disabled:       /* Muted text */
--eevenkoto-color-control-[variant]-border-disabled:     /* Structural stroke */
```

**Decorative Surface Exemption:** Surfaces that never host text (e.g., backdrop dimming scrims) may opt out of the text-coupling requirement with an inline annotation:

```css
/* stylelint-disable-next-line eevenkoto/require-text-tuple */
--eevenkoto-color-surface-backdrop: color-mix(
  in oklch,
  var(--eevenkoto-color-parchment-text) 60%,
  transparent
);
```

**Planned enforcement:** AST linting should require every token ending in `-background` to have a co-located `-text` sibling within the same selector (not wired yet).

### 3.3 Ban on `-inverse` Tokens (Scoped Context Theming)

**Rule:** Do not create `-inverse` tokens (e.g., `--eevenkoto-color-content-inverse`).

**Rationale:** Adding `-inverse` creates an explosion of parallel tokens when dark containers host complex children (inputs, tables, tooltips).

**Implementation:** Apply Scoped Context Theming using `[data-surface-mode="dark"]`. The cascade rebinds the standard tokens locally:

```css
/* Inverted surface container rebinds standard tokens locally */
[data-surface-mode="dark"] {
  --eevenkoto-color-surface-canvas:  var(--eevenkoto-color-obsidian-background);
  --eevenkoto-color-content-primary: var(--eevenkoto-color-obsidian-text);
  --eevenkoto-color-link-default:    var(--eevenkoto-color-turquoise-primary);
  --eevenkoto-color-boundary-subtle: var(--eevenkoto-color-obsidian-border-subtle);
}
```

**Planned enforcement:** AST linting should reject any token name containing the substring `-inverse` (not wired yet).

### 3.4 Contrast & Polarity Standards

Token pairings must pass two automated CI checks:

**WCAG 2.1/2.2 AA (sRGB Relative Luminance Y):**

- Normal text: ≥ 4.5:1
- Large text & non-text UI components: ≥ 3.0:1

**APCA Directional Lightness (L<sup>c</sup>):**

- Dark text on light background (positive polarity): L<sup>c</sup> ≥ +75
- Light text on dark background (negative polarity): L<sup>c</sup> ≥ −60 (prevents halation fatigue)
- Non-text graphics & boundaries: |L<sup>c</sup>| ≥ 45

#### Contrast Requirements by Element Type

- **Contained Controls (Buttons):** Internal contrast between background and text must meet ≥ 4.5:1.
- **Inline Links:** Must meet ≥ 4.5:1 against the ambient surface and ≥ 3.0:1 against adjacent body text.
- **Form Controls:** Checkbox/radio tracks and input borders must meet ≥ 3.0:1 non-text contrast against the canvas.
- **Dual-Boundary Focus Indicators:** A single focus ring cannot guarantee contrast against both an arbitrary control fill and an unknown outer canvas. Tier 2 defines a two-part halo:
  - `--eevenkoto-color-boundary-focus-outer`: Contrasts against the surrounding canvas (≥ 3.0:1).
  - `--eevenkoto-color-boundary-focus-inner`: Contrasts against the component's inner fill (≥ 3.0:1).
- **Multi-Canvas Surface Rule:** Because typography renders across multiple elevation steps, `--eevenkoto-color-content-primary` must clear WCAG AA (≥ 4.5:1) against `--eevenkoto-color-surface-canvas`, `--eevenkoto-color-surface-subtle`, and `--eevenkoto-color-surface-sunken`.

### 3.5 Elevation & Depth Mechanics

**Light Mode (Subtractive Elevation):** Canvas separation relies on subtle borders and drop shadows tinted with ink pigments:

```css
--eevenkoto-color-depth-shadow-umbra: color-mix(
  in oklch,
  var(--eevenkoto-color-parchment-text) 12%,
  transparent
);
--eevenkoto-color-depth-shadow-penumbra: color-mix(
  in oklch,
  var(--eevenkoto-color-parchment-text) 6%,
  transparent
);
```

**Dark Mode (Additive Elevation):** Black shadows are invisible against dark canvas. Elevation is communicated by stepping lightness (L) upward:

- Canvas Root: obsidian wash (L ≈ 0.14)
- Raised Surface (Cards, Rows): obsidian subtle (L ≈ 0.18)
- Sunken Surface (Inputs, Wells): obsidian base (L ≈ 0.10)

## Canonical Semantic Token Definitions

Illustrative excerpts for `tokens.css`. Theme switching occurs only in this layer.

```css
/* ==========================================================================
   TIER 2: SEMANTIC TOKENS (tokens.css)
   Exclusively references Tier 1 primitives or oklch color-mix expressions.
   ========================================================================== */

:root {
  /* 1. SURFACES & DEPTH (Light Mode - Subtractive Model) */
  --eevenkoto-color-surface-canvas:        var(--eevenkoto-color-parchment-background);
  --eevenkoto-color-surface-subtle:        var(--eevenkoto-color-parchment-background-subtle);
  --eevenkoto-color-surface-sunken:        var(--eevenkoto-color-parchment-background-element);
  --eevenkoto-color-surface-raised:        var(--eevenkoto-color-parchment-background);

  --eevenkoto-color-depth-shadow-umbra:    color-mix(
    in oklch,
    var(--eevenkoto-color-parchment-text) 12%,
    transparent
  );
  --eevenkoto-color-depth-shadow-penumbra: color-mix(
    in oklch,
    var(--eevenkoto-color-parchment-text) 6%,
    transparent
  );

  /* 2. CONTENT & TYPOGRAPHY */
  --eevenkoto-color-content-primary:       var(--eevenkoto-color-parchment-text);
  --eevenkoto-color-content-secondary:     var(--eevenkoto-color-parchment-text-muted);
  --eevenkoto-color-content-tertiary:      var(--eevenkoto-color-parchment-text-subtle);
  --eevenkoto-color-content-accent:        var(--eevenkoto-color-parchment-primary);
  --eevenkoto-color-content-accent-strong: var(--eevenkoto-color-gold-primary-deep);
  --eevenkoto-color-content-disabled:      var(--eevenkoto-color-parchment-border);

  /* 3. TYPOGRAPHIC LINKS */
  --eevenkoto-color-link-default:          var(--eevenkoto-color-turquoise-state);
  --eevenkoto-color-link-hover:            var(--eevenkoto-color-turquoise-state-hover);
  --eevenkoto-color-link-underline:        color-mix(
    in oklch,
    var(--eevenkoto-color-link-default) 40%,
    transparent
  );

  /* 4. BOUNDARIES & FOCUS */
  --eevenkoto-color-boundary-subtle:       color-mix(
    in oklch,
    var(--eevenkoto-color-parchment-border) 35%,
    transparent
  );
  --eevenkoto-color-boundary-strong:       var(--eevenkoto-color-parchment-border);
  --eevenkoto-color-boundary-focus-outer:  var(--eevenkoto-color-gold-primary);
  --eevenkoto-color-boundary-focus-inner:  var(--eevenkoto-color-surface-canvas);

  /* 5. CONTROLS: PRIMARY ACTION */
  --eevenkoto-color-control-primary-background:          var(--eevenkoto-color-turquoise-state);
  --eevenkoto-color-control-primary-background-hover:    var(--eevenkoto-color-turquoise-state-hover);
  --eevenkoto-color-control-primary-background-active:   var(--eevenkoto-color-turquoise-state-hover);
  --eevenkoto-color-control-primary-text:                var(--eevenkoto-color-turquoise-text);
  --eevenkoto-color-control-primary-border:              transparent;

  --eevenkoto-color-control-primary-background-disabled: var(--eevenkoto-color-parchment-background-element);
  --eevenkoto-color-control-primary-text-disabled:       var(--eevenkoto-color-parchment-border);
  --eevenkoto-color-control-primary-border-disabled:     transparent;

  /* 6. CONTROLS: DESTRUCTIVE ACTION */
  --eevenkoto-color-control-destructive-background:          var(--eevenkoto-color-crimson-state);
  --eevenkoto-color-control-destructive-background-hover:    var(--eevenkoto-color-crimson-state-hover);
  --eevenkoto-color-control-destructive-text:                var(--eevenkoto-color-crimson-text);
  --eevenkoto-color-control-destructive-border:              transparent;

  /* 7. FORM INPUTS & VALIDATION TUPLE */
  --eevenkoto-color-form-input-background:         var(--eevenkoto-color-parchment-background);
  --eevenkoto-color-form-input-text:               var(--eevenkoto-color-parchment-text);
  --eevenkoto-color-form-input-border:             var(--eevenkoto-color-parchment-border);

  --eevenkoto-color-form-input-background-invalid: var(--eevenkoto-color-crimson-tint-cool);
  --eevenkoto-color-form-input-text-invalid:       var(--eevenkoto-color-crimson-text);
  --eevenkoto-color-form-input-border-invalid:     var(--eevenkoto-color-crimson-state);
  --eevenkoto-color-form-input-message-invalid:    var(--eevenkoto-color-crimson-text);

  /* 8. FEEDBACK CONTAINERS — subtle via color-mix; solid via state + on-fill text */
  --eevenkoto-color-feedback-caution-background: color-mix(
    in oklch,
    var(--eevenkoto-color-orange-state) 16%,
    transparent
  );
  --eevenkoto-color-feedback-caution-border: color-mix(
    in oklch,
    var(--eevenkoto-color-orange-state) 30%,
    transparent
  );
  --eevenkoto-color-feedback-caution-text: color-mix(
    in oklch,
    var(--eevenkoto-color-orange-state) 65%,
    var(--eevenkoto-color-parchment-text)
  );

  --eevenkoto-color-feedback-critical-background: color-mix(
    in oklch,
    var(--eevenkoto-color-crimson-state) 14%,
    transparent
  );
  --eevenkoto-color-feedback-critical-border: color-mix(
    in oklch,
    var(--eevenkoto-color-crimson-state) 28%,
    transparent
  );
  --eevenkoto-color-feedback-critical-text: color-mix(
    in oklch,
    var(--eevenkoto-color-crimson-state) 70%,
    var(--eevenkoto-color-parchment-text)
  );
}

/* ==========================================================================
   DARK THEME OVERRIDES ([data-theme="dark"])
   ========================================================================== */
[data-theme="dark"] {
  --eevenkoto-color-surface-canvas:   var(--eevenkoto-color-obsidian-background);
  --eevenkoto-color-surface-sunken:   var(--eevenkoto-color-obsidian-background-element);
  --eevenkoto-color-surface-raised:   var(--eevenkoto-color-obsidian-background-subtle);

  --eevenkoto-color-content-primary:  var(--eevenkoto-color-obsidian-text);
  --eevenkoto-color-content-secondary: var(--eevenkoto-color-obsidian-text-muted);

  --eevenkoto-color-link-default:     var(--eevenkoto-color-turquoise-primary);
  --eevenkoto-color-link-hover:       var(--eevenkoto-color-turquoise-text);

  --eevenkoto-color-control-primary-background:       var(--eevenkoto-color-turquoise-primary);
  --eevenkoto-color-control-primary-background-hover: var(--eevenkoto-color-turquoise-primary-hover);
  --eevenkoto-color-control-primary-text:             var(--eevenkoto-color-turquoise-tint-deep);
}
```

## CI enforcement

These Stylelint rules and contrast checks run in `npm run lint:css`, `npm run contrast`, and `npm run ci`.

| Check | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Zero Raw Literals | Rejects raw color formats in `tokens.css`. Allowed: primitive `var()`, constrained `color-mix(in oklch, …)` recipes (fades / disabled endpoints — see §3.1a), platform keywords, system colors. |
| Mandatory Text Tuples | Requires any selector declaring a `-background` property to include a matching `-text` property, unless annotated with `/* stylelint-disable-next-line eevenkoto/require-text-tuple */`. |
| Mandatory Disabled Tuples | Requires interactive variants with `-background-disabled` to also declare `-text-disabled` and `-border-disabled`. |
| Banned `-inverse` Names | Scans for `-inverse` in token names and fails the build. Use scoped context containers instead. |
| Dual-Canvas Contrast Audits | Verifies `--eevenkoto-color-content-primary` meets WCAG AA (≥ 4.5:1) against `--eevenkoto-color-surface-canvas`, `--eevenkoto-color-surface-subtle`, and `--eevenkoto-color-surface-sunken` across all themes. |
| Tier Isolation | Rejects any occurrence of Tier 1 primitive leakage patterns in `packages/css/core/` and `packages/css/domain/`. |
## Tier 3 — Component scoping

_Source: `apps/storybook/src/foundations/color-tokens-tier3-component-scoping.mdx`_

# Tier 3: Component Scoping & Token Architecture

**Audience:** authors writing component CSS in this repo — not app consumers. App usage: [Tokens catalog](/?path=/docs/foundations-tokens--docs) and repo `llms-full.txt`. Contributor rules: root `AGENTS.md`.

**Doc set:** [Architecture](./color-tokens-architecture.mdx) → [Tier 1 Primitives](./color-tokens-tier1-primitives.mdx) → [Tier 2 Semantics](./color-tokens-tier2-semantics.mdx) → Tier 3 Component Scoping (this file)

This document defines the architectural mechanics, naming grammar, encapsulation contracts, and governance rules for the component token layer (Tier 3). Tier 3 bridges Tier 2 semantic tokens into scoped, override-resilient component implementations without specificity wars or cascading side effects.

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Source file | `packages/css/core/...` or `packages/css/domain/...` (atoms / molecules / organisms) |
| Public API | `--eevenkoto-<component>-[element]-[property]-[state]` |
| Private bridge | `--_eevenkoto-<component>-[element]-[property]` |

## Architectural Scope & The Encapsulation Contract

The Eevenkoto token architecture decouples physical color physics (Tier 1) and intent orchestration (Tier 2) from DOM element boundaries (Tier 3).

```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Tier 1: Primitives (primitive-tokens.css)                        │
│  --eevenkoto-color-<hue>-<function>                              │
│  Sparse, hue-specific OKLCH pigment jars                         │
└────────────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────┘
                                 │ Mapped per theme / context
                                 ▼
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Tier 2: Semantics (tokens.css)                                  │
│  --eevenkoto-color-[domain]-[variant]-[element]-[state]          │
│  Cross-hue composition, intent tuples, & contrast enforcement    │
└────────────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────┘
                                 │ Consumed as fallback defaults
                                 ▼
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Tier 3: Component Scoping (packages/css/core or domain)         │
│  --eevenkoto-<component>-[element]-[property]-[state] (Public)   │
│  --_eevenkoto-<component>-[element]-[property]        (Private)  │
│  Encapsulated DOM boundaries, private bridges, & context hooks   │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### The Division of Concerns

| Tier | Answers |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | What does this pigment look like across its physical optical curve? |
| 2 | What role does this color play in the interface, and which counter-ink guarantees accessibility? |
| 3 | Which DOM element surface consumes which semantic intent, how do sub-elements interact, and how can parent layouts contextualize this component without breaking encapsulation? |

### The Encapsulation Guarantee

A production UI component must behave as a sealed mechanical unit. It manages its own internal geometry, layout, hitboxes, and accessibility state indicators. It exposes a minimal, explicit public API for contextual theming and style overrides while remaining completely immune to accidental parent cascade bleeding.

## The Two-Layer Underscore Bridge Pattern

Consuming CSS variables directly inside properties (e.g., `background-color: var(--eevenkoto-color-control-primary-background)`) creates two systemic flaws:

1. **Zero Override Ergonomics:** External consumers must either write high-specificity CSS overrides or redefine a global semantic variable, risking unintended sibling/child fallout.
2. **The Cyclic Invalidation Trap (IACVT):** If a component accepts an override via the same variable name it assigns (`--eevenkoto-button-bg: var(--eevenkoto-button-bg, ...)`), CSS Custom Property resolution flags a cyclic dependency. At computed-value time the variable becomes Invalid at Computed-Value Time (IACVT) and resolves to `unset`.

### The Private Bridge Pattern (`--_`)

Every component styles its DOM using a three-tier assignment cycle:

1. **Public Custom Property API:** `--eevenkoto-<component>-[element]-[property]`
2. **Private Internal Bridge Property:** `--_eevenkoto-<component>-[element]-[property]`
3. **CSS Spec Property Declaration:** `property: var(--_eevenkoto-...)`

```css
/* Canonical Tier 3 Implementation */
.eevenkoto-button {
  /* 1. PRIVATE BRIDGE DECLARATIONS
     Read from public override API; fall back to Tier 2 semantic tokens. */
  --_eevenkoto-button-bg: var(
    --eevenkoto-button-bg,
    var(--eevenkoto-color-control-primary-background)
  );
  --_eevenkoto-button-text: var(
    --eevenkoto-button-text,
    var(--eevenkoto-color-control-primary-text)
  );
  --_eevenkoto-button-border-color: var(
    --eevenkoto-button-border-color,
    var(--eevenkoto-color-control-primary-border)
  );

  /* 2. PROPERTY ATTACHMENT
     Attach ONLY private bridge variables to standard CSS properties. */
  background-color: var(--_eevenkoto-button-bg);
  color: var(--_eevenkoto-button-text);
  border-color: var(--_eevenkoto-button-border-color);
}
```

### How the Engine Resolves the Bridge

```text
Parent passes public override?
      │
      ├─► YES: --eevenkoto-button-bg is defined ──► --_eevenkoto-button-bg takes override value
      │
      └─► NO:  --eevenkoto-button-bg is missing ─► --_eevenkoto-button-bg resolves Tier 2 fallback
```

Because the public variable and the private variable have distinct identifiers, no cycle exists. The component provides guaranteed fallback behavior while exposing a declarative, zero-specificity override hook.

## Naming Grammar & Token Anatomy

### Public Override API Grammar

```text
--eevenkoto-[component]-[element]-[property]-[state]
```

| Token Segment | Description | Examples |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--eevenkoto-` | System root prefix. Identifies official design system tokens. | `--eevenkoto-` |
| `[component]` | Canonical component identifier in kebab-case. | `button`, `text-input`, `card`, `modal` |
| `[element]` | Optional sub-element or slot. Omitted if target is root container. | `label`, `input`, `indicator`, `track`, `thumb`, `icon` |
| `[property]` | Exact visual or geometric property being manipulated. | `bg`, `text`, `border-color`, `radius`, `pad-block`, `pad-inline` |
| `[state]` | Optional interactive or structural state. Omitted for default resting state. | `hover`, `active`, `focus`, `disabled`, `invalid`, `checked` |

### Private Internal Bridge Grammar

```text
--_eevenkoto-[component]-[element]-[property]
```

- The underscore prefix (`--_`) denotes a private variable scoped strictly to the component's internal stylesheet.
- Private bridges must never appear in external consumer stylesheets.
- Private bridges are declared **once on the host class**. Variants and states must never reassign `--_*`; they set the public `--eevenkoto-*` API that the bridge already reads.
- Private bridges must never have states in their identifier names; states assign public resting tokens (optionally fed by a state-suffixed public override such as `--eevenkoto-button-bg-hover`).

## The 4 Strict Scoping Rules

### Rule 1: Strict Tier Isolation (No Tier 1 Leakage)

A component stylesheet must never reference a Tier 1 primitive by hue (e.g., `--eevenkoto-color-turquoise-*`).

- **Violation:** `background-color: var(--eevenkoto-color-turquoise-state);`
- **Correction:** Reference the semantic intent: `var(--eevenkoto-color-control-primary-background)`.
- **Planned enforcement:** Stylelint should block hue-primitive leakage in component stylesheets under `packages/css/core/**` and `packages/css/domain/**` (not wired in CI yet — follow the rule manually).

### Rule 2: Complete Tuple Synchronization on State & Variant Shifts

When a component variant, pseudo-class (`:hover`, `:active`, `:focus-visible`), or state (`:disabled`, `[aria-invalid="true"]`) alters a surface background token, it is mandatory to rebind the matching text and border tokens within the exact same rule block — by setting the **public** `--eevenkoto-*` API, not the private bridges.

- **Failure Mode:** Overriding `--eevenkoto-button-bg` on hover without updating `--eevenkoto-button-text` causes local contrast collapse when a theme or variant changes.
- **Standard:** Rebind the entire public tuple simultaneously.

### Rule 3: No Downward or Sibling Leakage

- Component tokens are scoped to their component host class (`.eevenkoto-<component>`).
- Component stylesheets must not define global selectors (`:root`, `body`, `div`).
- Modifiers must be applied via BEM-style variant classes (e.g., `.eevenkoto-button--secondary`) or data attributes (`data-variant="secondary"`), never via bare tag selectors.
- **Exception (type only):** Heading may map level from the host tag with `:where(hN).eevenkoto-heading` (zero tag specificity so `--M` still overrides). Bare `h1`–`h6` / `p` styling is allowed only under the Prose host (`.eevenkoto-prose :where(…)`). Do not style those tags globally.
- **Host defaults:** The host class alone must implement the documented default (see [Minimum-class defaults](/?path=/docs/foundations-minimum-class-defaults--docs)). Default variant/size modifiers are optional aliases, not requirements.

### Rule 4: Zero Speculative Property Exposure

Do not author public override tokens for CSS properties the component does not actively support. If a component does not explicitly govern `line-height` or `transform`, do not declare `--eevenkoto-button-line-height`. Expose only verified geometric, color, and depth parameters.

## State & Variant Mechanics

Variants and states should not duplicate the full declaration list of a component. They set the **public** override API; the host’s private bridges keep reading those publics and feed CSS properties.

```text
       ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
       │                 .eevenkoto-button (Base)                     │
       │  --_eevenkoto-button-bg: var(--eevenkoto-button-bg, …);      │
       │  --_eevenkoto-button-text: var(--eevenkoto-button-text, …);  │
       │  background-color: var(--_eevenkoto-button-bg);              │
       │  color: var(--_eevenkoto-button-text);                       │
       └─────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────┘
                                     │
           ┌─────────────────────────┴─────────────────────────┐
           ▼                                                   ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────┐ ┌───────────────────────────────────┐
│   .eevenkoto-button--secondary  │ │   .eevenkoto-button:hover         │
│   (Variant)                     │ │   (State)                         │
│   Sets --eevenkoto-button-* to  │ │   Sets --eevenkoto-button-* to    │
│   Secondary Tier 2 tokens.      │ │   hover Tier 2 (or *-hover API).  │
│   Does not touch --_* bridges.  │ │   Keeps bg/text/border coupled.   │
└─────────────────────────────────┘ └───────────────────────────────────┘
```

```css
/* Canonical: variants assign public API only */
.eevenkoto-button--secondary {
  --eevenkoto-button-bg: var(--eevenkoto-color-control-secondary-background);
  --eevenkoto-button-text: var(--eevenkoto-color-control-secondary-text);
  --eevenkoto-button-border-color: var(--eevenkoto-color-control-secondary-border);
}

/* Anti-pattern: do not rebind private bridges on variants */
.eevenkoto-button--secondary {
  --_eevenkoto-button-bg: var(
    --eevenkoto-button-bg,
    var(--eevenkoto-color-control-secondary-background)
  );
}
```

## Gradients as Tier 3 Composition

Tier 2 owns **solid** contrast tuples (`background` / `text` / `border` / `icon`). Multi-stop gradients, staggered stop transitions, and decorative elevation shadows are **Tier 3 recipes** — they ornament the solid fill; they do not replace the contrast contract.

### Rules

1. **Solid fill always exists.** On the host, bridge `--_eevenkoto-<component>-bg` to the public API with a Tier 2 `*-background` fallback, and attach the private bridge to `background-color`. Gradients attach via `background-image` so forced-colors / gradient stripping still leave a readable fill.
2. **Compose stops from Tier 2.** Default gradient stops with `color-mix(in display-p3, …)` over semantic tokens — never hue primitives, never raw `oklch()` in the component sheet.
3. **Public stop overrides.** Expose `--eevenkoto-<component>-gradient-{start,middle,end}` (and `-hover` / state variants when needed). Bridge through private `--_eevenkoto-<component>-gradient-*` on the host only.
4. **`@property` registers private bridges only.** Registering a public custom property with an `initial-value` makes `var(--public, fallback)` always take the initial value and kills Tier 2 fallbacks. Animate the private `--_*` names; variants/states change the public stop vars so the registered bridges recompute.
5. **States set the full public color tuple plus stops together.** Disabled states must use opaque disabled backgrounds as gradient stops (or `transparent` for ghost) — never `opacity` on the host.

```css
@property --_eevenkoto-button-gradient-start {
  syntax: "<color>";
  inherits: false;
  initial-value: transparent;
}

.eevenkoto-button {
  --_eevenkoto-button-bg: var(
    --eevenkoto-button-bg,
    var(--eevenkoto-color-control-primary-background)
  );
  --_eevenkoto-button-gradient-start: var(
    --eevenkoto-button-gradient-start,
    color-mix(
      in display-p3,
      var(--eevenkoto-color-control-primary-background),
      var(--eevenkoto-color-control-primary-background-hover) 30%
    )
  );
  --_eevenkoto-button-gradient-middle: var(
    --eevenkoto-button-gradient-middle,
    var(--eevenkoto-color-control-primary-background)
  );
  --_eevenkoto-button-gradient-end: var(
    --eevenkoto-button-gradient-end,
    color-mix(
      in display-p3,
      var(--eevenkoto-color-control-primary-background),
      var(--eevenkoto-color-control-primary-icon) 30%
    )
  );

  background-color: var(--_eevenkoto-button-bg);
  background-image: linear-gradient(
    328deg,
    var(--_eevenkoto-button-gradient-start) 0%,
    var(--_eevenkoto-button-gradient-end) 50%,
    var(--_eevenkoto-button-gradient-middle) 100%
  );
  transition:
    --_eevenkoto-button-gradient-start var(--eevenkoto-duration-1) var(--eevenkoto-ease-in-out),
    --_eevenkoto-button-gradient-middle var(--eevenkoto-duration-2) var(--eevenkoto-ease-in-out),
    --_eevenkoto-button-gradient-end var(--eevenkoto-duration-3) var(--eevenkoto-ease-in-out);
}
```

Parents override look without specificity wars:

```css
.hero-banner {
  --eevenkoto-button-gradient-start: var(--eevenkoto-color-control-secondary-background);
  --eevenkoto-button-gradient-middle: var(--eevenkoto-color-control-secondary-background);
  --eevenkoto-button-gradient-end: var(--eevenkoto-color-control-secondary-tint);
}
```

### Opaque Disabled State Implementation

Per Tier 2 architecture, `opacity: 0.5` is strictly banned. Tier 3 components must implement disabled states using opaque, non-bleeding semantic tokens:

```css
.eevenkoto-button:disabled,
.eevenkoto-button[aria-disabled="true"] {
  cursor: not-allowed;

  /* Set the complete public disabled tuple simultaneously */
  --eevenkoto-button-bg: var(
    --eevenkoto-button-bg-disabled,
    var(--eevenkoto-color-control-primary-background-disabled)
  );
  --eevenkoto-button-text: var(
    --eevenkoto-button-text-disabled,
    var(--eevenkoto-color-control-primary-text-disabled)
  );
  --eevenkoto-button-border-color: var(
    --eevenkoto-button-border-color-disabled,
    var(--eevenkoto-color-control-primary-border-disabled)
  );
}
```

## Contextual Theming & Parent-Child Override Protocols

When a parent container requires its child components to render in a distinct variant, developers must never write cross-component selector overrides.

### The Anti-Pattern (Selector Specificity Leaks)

```css
/* BANNED: Breaks button encapsulation, escalates specificity, breaks when button DOM refactors */
.hero-banner .eevenkoto-button {
  background-color: oklch(0.96 0.02 90) !important;
  color: oklch(0.18 0.02 85) !important;
}
```

### The Architectural Pattern (Declarative API Injection)

The parent container sets the child component's public override variables locally. The child's internal bridge resolves the override automatically without specificity wars:

```css
/* RECOMMENDED: Declarative, zero-specificity override */
.hero-banner {
  --eevenkoto-button-bg: var(--eevenkoto-color-control-secondary-background);
  --eevenkoto-button-text: var(--eevenkoto-color-control-secondary-text);
  --eevenkoto-button-border-color: var(--eevenkoto-color-control-secondary-border);
}
```

### Surface Context Switching (`data-surface-mode`)

When a component is embedded within a dark surface inside an otherwise light page, the system leverages Tier 2 Scoped Context Theming. The component's standard Tier 2 tokens automatically remap without requiring variant classes on the component:

```html
<!-- The button remains plain .eevenkoto-button; tokens adapt automatically -->
<aside class="marketing-callout" data-surface-mode="dark">
  <p class="callout-prose">Subscribe to our newsletter.</p>
  <button type="button" class="eevenkoto-button">Subscribe</button>
</aside>
```

## Platform Adaptations & Accessibility at Tier 3

### Dual-Halo Focus Indicators

Focus rings must achieve minimum non-text contrast (≥ 3.0:1) against both the inner button fill and the outer layout canvas. Tier 3 implements a synchronized dual-halo boundary using an offset outline coupled with a box-shadow:

```css
.eevenkoto-button:focus-visible {
  outline: 2px solid var(--eevenkoto-color-boundary-focus-outer);
  outline-offset: 2px;
  box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px var(--eevenkoto-color-boundary-focus-inner);
}
```

### Forced Colors Mode (Windows High Contrast)

In `@media (forced-colors: active)`, user-agent stylesheets strip author background colors and drop shadows. If an interactive element lacks an explicit border in standard mode, its hit boundaries disappear entirely.

**The Forced-Colors Guardrail:** Every interactive component must declare an explicit border width and style, utilizing `transparent` when an invisible border is desired in standard rendering. In Forced Colors mode, the browser automatically converts transparent borders into visible system `ButtonBorder` strokes:

```css
.eevenkoto-button {
  /* Explicit 1px border is invisible in standard mode, but preserves hit boundaries in HCM */
  border-width: 1px;
  border-style: solid;
  border-color: var(--_eevenkoto-button-border-color); /* Defaults to transparent for solid buttons */
}
```

## Canonical Component Implementations

### Component: Contained Interactive Control (Button)

`packages/css/core/atoms/button.css`

The live Button uses the private-bridge contract below **plus** the [Gradients as Tier 3 Composition](#gradients-as-tier-3-composition) recipe (animated stops, brand shadows, scoop corners). The excerpt shows the solid tuple and dual-halo focus; open the component stylesheet for the full gradient implementation.

```css
/* ==========================================================================
   EEVENKOTO DESIGN SYSTEM: BUTTON COMPONENT (TIER 3)
   ========================================================================== */

.eevenkoto-button {
  /* 1. PRIVATE BRIDGE INITIALIZATION (Primary Action Defaults) */
  --_eevenkoto-button-bg: var(
    --eevenkoto-button-bg,
    var(--eevenkoto-color-control-primary-background)
  );
  --_eevenkoto-button-text: var(
    --eevenkoto-button-text,
    var(--eevenkoto-color-control-primary-text)
  );
  --_eevenkoto-button-border-color: var(
    --eevenkoto-button-border-color,
    var(--eevenkoto-color-control-primary-border)
  );

  /* Geometry & Typography Tokens */
  --_eevenkoto-button-pad-block: var(--eevenkoto-button-pad-block, 0.625rem);
  --_eevenkoto-button-pad-inline: var(--eevenkoto-button-pad-inline, 1.25rem);
  --_eevenkoto-button-radius: var(--eevenkoto-button-radius, 0.375rem);
  --_eevenkoto-button-font-size: var(--eevenkoto-button-font-size, 0.875rem);
  --_eevenkoto-button-font-weight: var(--eevenkoto-button-font-weight, 600);

  /* 2. ELEMENT STYLING DECLARATIONS */
  display: inline-flex;
  align-items: center;
  justify-content: center;
  gap: 0.5rem;
  box-sizing: border-box;
  margin: 0;
  padding: var(--_eevenkoto-button-pad-block) var(--_eevenkoto-button-pad-inline);

  font-family: inherit;
  font-size: var(--_eevenkoto-button-font-size);
  font-weight: var(--_eevenkoto-button-font-weight);
  line-height: 1.2;
  text-decoration: none;
  white-space: nowrap;

  background-color: var(--_eevenkoto-button-bg);
  color: var(--_eevenkoto-button-text);

  /* Forced-Colors boundary guardrail: explicit 1px stroke */
  border: 1px solid var(--_eevenkoto-button-border-color);
  border-radius: var(--_eevenkoto-button-radius);

  cursor: pointer;
  user-select: none;
  transition:
    background-color var(--eevenkoto-duration-3) var(--eevenkoto-ease-standard),
    border-color var(--eevenkoto-duration-3) var(--eevenkoto-ease-standard),
    color var(--eevenkoto-duration-3) var(--eevenkoto-ease-standard);
}

/* INTERACTIVE STATES (Coupled public tuple updates) */

.eevenkoto-button:hover:not(:disabled) {
  --eevenkoto-button-bg: var(
    --eevenkoto-button-bg-hover,
    var(--eevenkoto-color-control-primary-background-hover)
  );
}

.eevenkoto-button:active:not(:disabled) {
  --eevenkoto-button-bg: var(
    --eevenkoto-button-bg-active,
    var(--eevenkoto-color-control-primary-background-active)
  );
}

.eevenkoto-button:focus-visible {
  outline: 2px solid var(--eevenkoto-color-boundary-focus-outer);
  outline-offset: 2px;
  box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px var(--eevenkoto-color-boundary-focus-inner);
}

.eevenkoto-button:disabled,
.eevenkoto-button[aria-disabled="true"] {
  cursor: not-allowed;
  --eevenkoto-button-bg: var(
    --eevenkoto-button-bg-disabled,
    var(--eevenkoto-color-control-primary-background-disabled)
  );
  --eevenkoto-button-text: var(
    --eevenkoto-button-text-disabled,
    var(--eevenkoto-color-control-primary-text-disabled)
  );
  --eevenkoto-button-border-color: var(
    --eevenkoto-button-border-color-disabled,
    var(--eevenkoto-color-control-primary-border-disabled)
  );
}

/* VARIANT: DESTRUCTIVE ACTION */

.eevenkoto-button--destructive {
  --eevenkoto-button-bg: var(--eevenkoto-color-control-destructive-background);
  --eevenkoto-button-text: var(--eevenkoto-color-control-destructive-text);
  --eevenkoto-button-border-color: var(--eevenkoto-color-control-destructive-border);
}

.eevenkoto-button--destructive:hover:not(:disabled) {
  --eevenkoto-button-bg: var(
    --eevenkoto-button-bg-hover,
    var(--eevenkoto-color-control-destructive-background-hover)
  );
}
```

### Component: Form Field (TextField)

```css
/* ==========================================================================
   EEVENKOTO DESIGN SYSTEM: TEXT FIELD COMPONENT (TIER 3)
   ========================================================================== */

.eevenkoto-field {

}

}

.eevenkoto-field__input {
  /* 1. PRIVATE BRIDGE INITIALIZATION */

    --eevenkoto-field-input-bg,
    var(--eevenkoto-color-form-input-background)
  );
  --_eevenkoto-field-input-text: var(
    --eevenkoto-field-input-text,

    --eevenkoto-field-input-border-color,
    var(--eevenkoto-color-form-input-border)
  );

.eevenkoto-field__input:focus {

  box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px var(--eevenkoto-color-boundary-focus-outer);

/* VALIDATION STATE: INVALID / ERROR TUPLE */

.eevenkoto-field__input[aria-invalid="true"] {
  --eevenkoto-field-input-bg: var(
    --eevenkoto-field-input-bg-invalid,
    var(--eevenkoto-color-form-input-background-invalid)
  );
  --eevenkoto-field-input-text: var(
    --eevenkoto-field-input-text-invalid,
    var(--eevenkoto-color-form-input-text-invalid)
  );
  --eevenkoto-field-input-border-color: var(
    --eevenkoto-field-input-border-color-invalid,
    var(--eevenkoto-color-form-input-border-invalid)
  );
}

.eevenkoto-field__message {
  font-size: 0.75rem;
  color: var(--eevenkoto-color-content-secondary);
}

.eevenkoto-field__message--error {
  color: var(--eevenkoto-color-form-input-message-invalid);
}
```

.eevenkoto-card {

  --_eevenkoto-card-bg: var(
    --eevenkoto-card-bg,
    var(--eevenkoto-color-surface-raised)
  );
