
## CI verification & linting rules

These AST-based Stylelint checks run on `packages/css/core/**/*.css` and `packages/css/domain/**/*.css` via `npm run lint:css` / `npm run ci`.

```text
                    Pull Request / Code Commit
                                │
                                ▼
         ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │       Check 1: Primitive Prefix Check        │
         │  Does file contain hue-primitive leakage?    │
         └──────────────────────┬───────────────────────┘
                                │ NO
                                ▼
         ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │          Check 2: Raw Color Literals         │
         │ Does file contain #hex, rgb(), or oklch()?   │
         └──────────────────────┬───────────────────────┘
                                │ NO
                                ▼
         ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │     Check 3: Direct Tier 2 in Property       │
         │  Is CSS property set to var(--eevenkoto-color│
         │        WITHOUT a private bridge (--_)?       │
         └──────────────────────┬───────────────────────┘
                                │ NO
                                ▼
         ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │     Check 4: Cyclic Dependency Detection     │
         │   Is a public token assigned to itself?      │
         └──────────────────────┬───────────────────────┘
                                │ NO
                                ▼
                     [CI VALIDATION PASSED]
```

1. **Strict Tier 1 Boundary Guard** (`eevenkoto/no-primitive-in-components`) — Rejects hue-primitive references inside `packages/css/core/` and `packages/css/domain/`.
2. **Raw Literal Guard** (`eevenkoto/no-raw-color-literals`) — Rejects raw hex, `rgb()`, `hsl()`, or `oklch()` literals within component stylesheets.
3. **Bridge Enforcement** (`eevenkoto/enforce-private-bridge`) — Flags component CSS that consumes a Tier 2 token without establishing the private `--_eevenkoto-` bridge fallback pattern.
4. **Cyclic Invalidation Guard** (`eevenkoto/no-self-referencing-vars`) — Flags assignments where a public token references itself without a separate private variable.

```css
/* CI FAILS THIS: Cyclic invalidation (IACVT) */
--eevenkoto-button-bg: var(--eevenkoto-button-bg, red);

/* CI PASSES THIS: Distinct private variable */
--_eevenkoto-button-bg: var(--eevenkoto-button-bg, red);
```
## Component taxonomy

_Source: `apps/storybook/src/foundations/component-taxonomy.mdx`_

# Component taxonomy

Eevenkoto organizes UI on **two axes**:

1. **Reuse scope** — **Core** (product-agnostic chrome) vs **Domain** (Eevenkoto content vocabulary: creatures, abilities, statblocks).
2. **Composition level** — Atomic Design: **Atoms → Molecules → Organisms**. Templates and Pages are reserved for later full-page demos.

Also read: [Glossary](/?path=/docs/foundations-glossary--docs) · [Packages](/?path=/docs/foundations-packages--docs) · [Authoring composed components](/?path=/docs/foundations-authoring-composed-components--docs)

## Why both axes

Atomic levels answer “how complex is this?” They do **not** answer “is this reusable chrome or creature content?” Core vs Domain keeps Button and Heading from looking interchangeable with Statblock in the sidebar and in source layout.

| Scope | Meaning | Examples |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Core** | Portable building blocks; English APIs; no RPG vocabulary required | Button, LinkButton, Badge, Heading, Property, List, Stat, Flow, Table, TableShell |
| **Domain** | Content patterns for this product family; may compose Core freely | EntityRef, AbilityScore, StatblockFeature, Statblock, Spellblock |

## Composition levels

| Level | Owns | Core examples | Domain examples |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Atom** | One semantic unit + BEM classes | Button, LinkButton, Badge, StatusDot, Chip, Heading, Paragraph, Caption, Property, ListItem, Stat, Frame, Scroll, TableCell, InlineRef | EntityRef |
| **Molecule** | Layout of atoms + local ARIA | Flow, Prose, PropertyList, List, Table, Menu, Catalog | AbilityScore, StatblockFeature, StatblockSection |
| **Organism** | Page-shaped composition, slots, outline | TableShell | AbilityScoreGroup, Statblock, Spellblock |

Prop and file naming: see [Glossary](/?path=/docs/foundations-glossary--docs).

## Dependency rule

**Domain may import Core. Core must never import Domain.**

Promote a Domain piece into Core only when reuse is proven across unrelated contexts — never because one screen needs it.

## Source layout

Package source mirrors the taxonomy (`core/atoms/…`, `domain/organisms/…`) while root barrels (`@eevenkoto/html`, `@eevenkoto/react`, …) keep a stable public export surface.

Storybook titles follow the same paths: `Core/Atoms/Button`, `Domain/Organisms/Statblock`.
## Glossary

_Source: `apps/storybook/src/foundations/glossary.mdx`_

# Glossary

Canonical vocabulary for Eevenkoto APIs, source layout, and docs. Prefer these names in props, types, file paths, and prose.

Also read: [Component taxonomy](/?path=/docs/foundations-component-taxonomy--docs) · [Authoring composed components](/?path=/docs/foundations-authoring-composed-components--docs) · [Minimum-class defaults](/?path=/docs/foundations-minimum-class-defaults--docs) · [Packages](/?path=/docs/foundations-packages--docs) (Button vs LinkButton chooser for agents)

## Locale policy

- **Public APIs are English** (prop names, type names, BEM blocks, defaults).
- **Product-language strings are data** — Finnish (or any locale) belongs in story / app props, not in `@eevenkoto/core`.
- English defaults (`Score`, `Modifier`, `Save`, `proficient`) may ship for AT labels; override them when the surrounding UI is localized (`scoreLabel`, `modifierLabel`, `saveLabel`, `proficientLabel`).

## Architecture terms

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **Core** | Product-agnostic chrome; no RPG vocabulary required |
| **Domain** | Eevenkoto content patterns (creatures, abilities, statblocks); may compose Core |
| **Atom** | One semantic unit + BEM classes |
| **Molecule** | Layout of atoms + local ARIA |
| **Organism** | Page-shaped composition, slots, outline |
| **Tier 1 / 2 / 3** | Token layers: primitives → semantics → component bridges |
| **Host default** | `.eevenkoto-<block>` alone = documented default look; see [Minimum-class defaults](/?path=/docs/foundations-minimum-class-defaults--docs) |
| **Prose** | Scope for bare `h1`–`h6` / `p` / `ul` / `ol` / `li` type styles (compose with Flow for rhythm) |
| **Flow** | Vertical rhythm for stacked type (classed or Prose+Flow bare tags) |

## Domain entry stack

| Term | Meaning | Prop / type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Statblock** | Creature / entity **entry** organism | `StatblockProps` |
| **name** | Creature title | `name`, `nameLevel` |
| **flavor** | Optional lead paragraph | `flavor` |
| **typeLine** | Size / type caption | `typeLine` |
| **vitals** | Combat vitals PropertyList (AbilityScoreGroup **header**) | `vitals: PropertyItem[]` |
| **abilities** | Ability columns | `abilities: AbilityScoreProps[]` |
| **details** | Skills, gear, senses, languages, CR (AbilityScoreGroup **footer**) | `details: PropertyItem[]` |
| **section** | Named block (Actions, Reactions, …) | `StatblockSectionProps.title` |
| **feature** | Named action / trait / reaction line | `StatblockFeatureProps` (`name`, `description`) |
| **AbilityScore** | One ability column (label + score + modifier + save) | `AbilityScoreProps` |
| **AbilityScoreGroup** | Sandwich organism (header + grid + footer) | `AbilityScoreGroupProps` |

Do **not** use **traits** for the footer PropertyList — that word collides with feature-style “traits” in rules prose. The footer rail is **`details`**.

## Domain spell entry

| Term | Meaning | Prop / type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Spellblock** | Spell **entry** organism (banded card) | `SpellblockProps` |
| **typeLine** | Level + school line, italic on the title plate | `typeLine` |
| **classes** | Optional catalog rail (classes that grant the spell) | `classes: PropertyItem[]` |
| **properties** | Casting time, range, components, duration — the boxed stat band | `properties: PropertyItem[]` |
| **paragraphs** | Effect prose, one entry per paragraph | `paragraphs` |
| **features** | Scaling entries (higher-level slot, cantrip upgrade) | `StatblockFeatureProps[]` |
| **deck** | Compact card variant for spell grids | `deck` |

Spellblock reuses **StatblockFeature** for scaling run-ins; there is no separate spell-feature molecule. Spell entries have no named **sections** — 5.5e prints no section title inside a spell, so the bands are visual only and the scaling run-in itself takes the H2 directly under the spell name.

## Core display terms

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **Property** | One label → value pair (`dt` / `dd`) |
| **PropertyList** | Stacked properties (`dl`) — Core **molecule** |
| **ListItem** | One content-list row (`li`) |
| **List** | Stacked content items (`ul` / `ol`) — Core **molecule** (not PropertyList) |
| **Stat** | Numeric display chip (`disk` / `arch` / `shield`) |
| **StatusDot** | Unlabeled readiness pip (same intents as Badge) |
| **Chip** | Interactive control chip (`selected`) |
| **Catalog** | Dense index grid of CatalogTiles |
| **Popover** | Raised floating panel chrome (CSS only; app owns open/position) |
| **TooltipCard** | Header / body / footer chrome nested in Popover (or standalone) — native `header` / `footer`, self-capping scroll body; not an in-page Card |
| **Card** | In-page sectioned surface (`article` + native `header` / flow / `footer`) |
| **InlineRef** | Core inline reference chrome (`name`, optional `href`); Popover trigger in Core demos |
| **Input** | Single-line **control chrome** only (fill / border / focus). Nest inside Field for forms. Uses `ariaLabel`, not `label`. |
| **Field** | Form **row**: visible `label` + control slot + hint/error. Default choice for data entry. |
| **emphasis** | Generic Stat highlight (thicker stroke, etc.) |
| **saveProficient** | Domain flag on AbilityScore; maps to Stat `emphasis` + AT suffix |

## Domain inline terms

| Term | Meaning | Prop / type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **EntityRef** | Domain specialization of InlineRef with closed kinds | `EntityRefProps` (`name`, `kind`, `href?`, `unlinked?`, `locked?`) |
| **kind** | Closed EntityRef taxonomy (`condition`, `mechanic`, `classFeature`, `class`, `spell`, `item`, `creature`) | `EntityRefKind` |
| **unlinked** | Known term with no page (InlineRef / EntityRef) | `unlinked` |
| **locked** | Gated destination; trailing lock Icon | `locked`, `lockedLabel` |

**Stat** (chip) and **Statblock** (entry) are different concepts that share a root word on purpose.

## Visible-string props

Use the prop that matches the role — do not force one name everywhere.

| Prop | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `label` | Visible control/chrome copy and definition terms (Button, LinkButton, Badge, Property, AbilityScore header, **Field** visible label). **Not** used on Input. |
| `ariaLabel` | Input-only: `aria-label` when there is no Field / visible label (chrome search). |
| `text` | Typography primitives (Heading, Paragraph, Caption, ListItem, TableCell body) |
| `name` | Named entity or inline reference (Statblock creature, Spellblock spell, StatblockFeature, InlineRef, EntityRef) |
| `title` | Section heading (StatblockSection, TooltipCard header) |
| `value` | Numeric or definitional payload (Stat, Property) |
| `description` | Feature body after the run-in name |
| `content` | HTML-only string body for composed hosts (Flow, Popover panel); React/Vue use `children` / slots |

In markup, a Property `label` is the definition **term** (`dt`). The prop name stays **`label`**.

## Variant vocabulary

| Surface | Prop | Values mean |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Button | `variant` | Action hierarchy: `primary` / `secondary` / `ghost` |
| LinkButton | `variant` | CTA hierarchy: `primary` / `secondary` (no ghost — in-prose links stay InlineRef) |
| Badge | `variant` | Surface recipe: `subtle` / `solid` / `outline` |
| Badge | `intent` | Feedback severity: `neutral` / `info` / `success` / `caution` / `critical` / `admin` |
| StatusDot | `intent` | Same feedback set; unlabeled pip |
| Chip | `selected` | Control selected / unselected |
| Heading / Paragraph / Caption / List | `tone` | Content weight: `primary` / `secondary` |
| List | `variant` | List kind: `unordered` / `ordered` |

`primary` is overloaded by design (control hierarchy vs content weight vs token slots). Prefer the table above over inventing parallel words.

Feedback uses **`caution`** / **`critical`** (not `warning` / `error`). Destructive actions use control **`destructive`** tokens / Button examples — that is separate from Badge intent.

## Button vs LinkButton vs InlineRef

Never put `href` on Button or wrap a Button in an `<a>`. Pick by **what happens**, not by how prominent it looks.

| Situation | Use |
| --- | --- |
| Hero / campaign “Start playing”, “Get the book”, “Read the rules” | **LinkButton** (`<a>`, required `href`) |
| Same-site page that is still a real URL | **LinkButton** |
| Form submit, dialog confirm, add/remove, open a modal or drawer | **Button** (`<button>`) |
| “Read more” or a term inside a paragraph | **InlineRef** (or a prose link) — not LinkButton |
| One main destination + one quieter destination | LinkButton **primary** + **secondary** (no ghost) |
| Destination is not ready | Omit the CTA; do not ship a disabled LinkButton as the only signal |

LinkButton looks related to Button on purpose (marketing CTAs) but stays a link: end-scoop shape, hover translate, no visited purple. Button is for **doing**; LinkButton is for **going**.

## Type layers

| Package | Canonical type name |
| --- | --- |
| `@eevenkoto/core` | `*Props` + `*ClassNames()` |
| `@eevenkoto/html` | `*Props` (HTML-only extensions stay as local `*Props` that extend core) |
| `@eevenkoto/react` | `*ComponentProps` (DOM attrs + core props) |
| `@eevenkoto/vue` | `*Props` on the component |

Do not introduce `*Args` aliases.

## File-name conventions

| Surface | Convention | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Core TS sources | camelCase | `abilityScore.ts` |
| CSS / HTML folders & files | kebab-case | `ability-score/`, `primitive-tokens.css` |
| React / Vue / Storybook components | PascalCase | `AbilityScore.tsx` |
| BEM blocks | `eevenkoto-<block>` | `eevenkoto-ability-score` |
| camelCase props → BEM modifiers | kebab-case | `saveProficient` → `--save-proficient`, `runIn` → `--run-in` |

Public CSS import paths stay flat (`@eevenkoto/css/ability-score.css`) even when source lives under `core/` or `domain/`.

## Migration (0.1.x)

| Was | Use instead |
| --- | --- |
| `StatblockProps.traits` | `details` |
| HTML `*Args` (e.g. `ButtonArgs`) | `*Props` |
| Bare `StatblockFeature` / `StatblockSection` type aliases | `StatblockFeatureProps` / `StatblockSectionProps` |
| `primitivetokens.css` (legacy filename) | `primitive-tokens.css` |
| PropertyList under `core/atoms/` | `core/molecules/` |
| AbilityScoreGroup under `domain/molecules/` | `domain/organisms/` |
## Authoring composed components

_Source: `apps/storybook/src/foundations/authoring-composed-components.mdx`_

# Authoring composed components

Patterns learned while porting the Statblock stack (Property → Stat → AbilityScore → Statblock). Use this when adding **Domain organisms** that compose Core atoms and molecules — not when tweaking a single Core control like Button.

Also read: [Glossary](/?path=/docs/foundations-glossary--docs) · [Component taxonomy](/?path=/docs/foundations-component-taxonomy--docs) · [Packages](/?path=/docs/foundations-packages--docs) · [Minimum-class defaults](/?path=/docs/foundations-minimum-class-defaults--docs) · [Color Tokens — Architecture](/?path=/docs/foundations-color-tokens-architecture--docs) · [Tier 3 — Component Scoping](/?path=/docs/foundations-color-tokens-tier-3-component-scoping--docs)

## 1. Decide scope and hierarchy before the CSS

Place each piece on **Core vs Domain**, then map **atom → molecule → organism**. Keep English APIs; leave **product-language strings as data**. Canonical prop names (`details` vs features, `label` vs `text` vs `name`) are in the [Glossary](/?path=/docs/foundations-glossary--docs).

| Scope | Layer | Statblock example | Owns |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Core | Atom | Property, Stat, Heading, Frame, Scroll, TableCell | One semantic unit + BEM classes |
| Core | Molecule | PropertyList, Table | Layout of atoms + local ARIA |
| Core | Organism | TableShell | Slots composing Frame + Scroll + Table (+ future Pager) |
| Domain | Molecule | AbilityScore, StatblockFeature | Layout of Core atoms + local ARIA |
| Domain | Organism | AbilityScoreGroup, Statblock, Spellblock | Page-shaped composition, slots, outline |

**Do:** Ship a working Domain organism against a real specimen (e.g. Aatelinen), then extract molecules once the seams are obvious.

**Don’t:** Invent Heading/Paragraph “product variants” for organism chrome. Visual remaps belong on the **molecule/organism host** (section looks like meso H3; feature run-in looks like micro H6) while **element levels stay honest**. Domain must not leak into Core source folders.

## 2. Keep the accessibility tree honest

| Rule | Why it mattered |
| --- | --- |
| Contiguous heading outline | Legacy H1 → H3 → H6 looked fine visually and broke structure. Prefer H1 → H2 → H3; remap *look* in CSS on the host. |
| Real landmarks and lists | `article` / `section`, real `dl` / `dt` / `dd` for definitional metadata. Use the Core **Table** ecosystem (`TableCell` → `Table` → `TableShell`) for true tabular charts — not bold-label paragraphs. |
| Name the group | Prefer `figure` / `figcaption` for a named unit; still wire `id` + `aria-labelledby` on the inner `dl` when the caption alone does not name the list. |
| Decorative punctuation in CSS | Colons and run-in periods via `::after`, not baked into copy strings. |
| Embed-safe outline props | Hardcoding H1 is correct for a dedicated entry page and wrong under a docs chrome H1. Expose something like `nameLevel?: 1 \| 2` when the organism owns a title. |

Screen-reader-only text belongs on a shared utility (`.eevenkoto-visually-hidden` with `clip-path: inset(50%)`), not ad-hoc `clip: rect(...)`.

## 3. Emphasis is never color alone

Status and proficiency cues must survive CVD, low vision, and **forced colors**.

1. **Redundant channel** — thicker stroke, outline, pattern, or visible mark *plus* an AT-facing term (`Save (proficient)`).
2. **Measure contrast on the real surface** — gold that passes on `surface-raised` / canvas can fail **1.4.11 (3:1)** on `surface-sunken`. Audit the panel the chip actually sits on.
3. **Prefer a new Tier 1 stop** when chrome needs a darker/lighter pigment (`gold-primary-deep`) — do not invent brand accents with hue×hue `color-mix` in Tier 2 ([Tier 1 — Prefer a new primitive](/?path=/docs/foundations-color-tokens-tier-1-primitives--docs)).
4. **Forced-colors** — strip decorative shadows; map borders to system colors (`ButtonText`, `Highlight` for emphasis). Interactive Tier 3 already requires explicit borders; content chips need the same habit.

## 4. Package checklist (every new piece)

Follow the same seam as Button / Badge / Statblock:

1. **`@eevenkoto/core`** — props + `*ClassNames()` (no DOM).
2. **`@eevenkoto/css`** — Tier 3 file; private `--_eevenkoto-*` bridges; public `--eevenkoto-<component>-*` overrides only.
3. **`@eevenkoto/html`** — canonical `render*` + template (Storybook source of truth).
4. **`@eevenkoto/react` / `@eevenkoto/vue`** — thin wrappers; prefer `ReactNode` / slots for rich text.
5. **Storybook** — specimen story from real product copy + MDX with **Why to use** (problem / motivation) before **When to use** (situations + Do/Don’t), plus outline, a11y, and framework notes.

HTML string → DOM is a **trust boundary**. If the HTML package accepts inline markup, **sanitize to an allowlist** (`em`, `strong`, `i`, `b`, `br`, …) and escape everything else. Framework wrappers should take nodes, not raw HTML strings.

## 5. Quick pre-merge checklist

- [ ] Heading levels match the document role; visuals remapped on the host, not via fake levels
- [ ] Lists / labels / values are programmatically associated (`dl`, `aria-labelledby`, etc.)
- [ ] Status/emphasis has a non-color cue + AT text where needed
- [ ] Non-text contrast checked on **sunken and raised** backgrounds the component uses
- [ ] `forced-colors` and `prefers-reduced-motion` considered
- [ ] Organism titles that might embed under another H1 have an escape hatch (`nameLevel` or equivalent)
- [ ] HTML renderer escapes / sanitizes; React/Vue don’t reintroduce `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` by default
- [ ] Public API is English; locale strings stay in story / product data
- [ ] Docs: **Why to use** explains the problem; **When to use** covers situations (do not put “Use X when…” only under Why)

## Reference specimen

[Statblock — Aatelinen](/?path=/docs/domain-organisms-statblock--docs) is the worked example: Core atoms (Property, Stat), Domain molecules (AbilityScore, StatblockFeature), Domain organisms (AbilityScoreGroup, Statblock), honest outline with visual remaps, proficiency emphasis, and embed `nameLevel`.

[Spellblock — Aavevalo](/?path=/docs/domain-organisms-spellblock--docs) is the second specimen, and shows two things Statblock does not: an organism that **owns its own card surface** (banded Tier 3 chrome instead of a flat stack), and a density variant driven by `container-type: inline-size` plus explicit wrapping rules for long Finnish compounds.
## Minimum-class defaults

_Source: `apps/storybook/src/foundations/minimum-class-defaults.mdx`_

# Minimum-class defaults

Every Tier 3 **host** (`.eevenkoto-<component>`) must look and behave as the **documented default** with no modifier classes. Modifiers are only for departing from that default. Framework `*ClassNames()` helpers may still emit explicit default aliases (`--primary`, `--md`, …) for a stable prop API.

Also read: [Tier 3 — Component Scoping](/?path=/docs/foundations-color-tokens-tier-3-component-scoping--docs) · [Typography](/?path=/docs/foundations-typography--docs) · [Packages](/?path=/docs/foundations-packages--docs) · [AGENTS.md](/AGENTS.md)

## Rules for authors

1. **Host = default.** Put the full default recipe (colors, size, interactive states, elevation) on `.eevenkoto-<block>`, via private-bridge fallbacks and host-level state selectors where needed.
2. **Modifiers are opt-in.** `--secondary`, `--sm`, `--solid`, etc. only change what is not already the default.
3. **Default modifier classes are aliases.** `--primary`, `--md`, `--subtle`, `--text`, `--stripe-row` may exist for helpers/docs but must not be *required* for the default look.
4. **Tag inference (type only).** Heading levels may come from `:where(hN).eevenkoto-heading` (zero tag specificity so `--M` still overrides). Do not use bare global `h1` / `p` / `button` selectors.
5. **Prose vs Flow.** Bare `h1`–`h6` / `p` / `ul` / `ol` / `li` get type styles only under `.eevenkoto-prose`. Vertical rhythm stays on `.eevenkoto-flow`. Compose: `eevenkoto-prose eevenkoto-flow`.
6. **Helpers may still be explicit.** Core can emit default modifiers so Button / Paragraph / List / Badge size props stay aligned; CSS must not depend on those classes for the default.

## Checklist when adding or changing a component

- [ ] `.eevenkoto-<block>` alone matches the Storybook default canvas
- [ ] Hover / focus / active / disabled for the default variant work without the default variant class
- [ ] Non-default variants fully override host defaults (no leaked primary hover, etc.)
- [ ] Docs show minimum markup (`class="eevenkoto-button"`, not only the fully expanded class list)
- [ ] If introducing “none” / opt-out (e.g. table stripe), emit an explicit modifier (`--stripe-none`) rather than relying on absence of a required default class

## Current defaults (hand-authored minimum)

| Host | Minimum markup | Default meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Heading | `<h2 class="eevenkoto-heading">` | Level from tag (`:where(hN)`); `--M` overrides |
| Paragraph | `<p class="eevenkoto-paragraph">` | `body-md` + primary |
| List | `<ul class="eevenkoto-list">` + bare `li` | unordered + `body-md` + primary (`ol` / `--ordered` for decimal); items via host descendants |
| Button | `<button class="eevenkoto-button">` | primary + md (full states) |
| LinkButton | `<a class="eevenkoto-link-button" href="…">` | primary + md + end-scoop (forward CTA link) |
| Badge | `<span class="eevenkoto-badge">` | subtle + neutral + md + pill |
| StatusDot | `<span class="eevenkoto-status-dot">` | neutral pip |
| Chip | `<button class="eevenkoto-chip">` | unselected + md |
| CatalogTile | `<a class="eevenkoto-catalog-tile" href="…">` | raised hairline row |
| Menu | `<nav class="eevenkoto-menu">` + `ul` / `li` / `a` | raised panel; rows from descendant `a` / `button` / `summary`; current page via `aria-current="page"` (`--embedded` flush sidebar) |
| Card | `<article class="eevenkoto-card">` + `header` / `p` / `footer` | flat raised surface; title look remapped on `header`; `--elevated` / `--interactive` opt-in |
| Badge intent | `eevenkoto-badge eevenkoto-badge--success` | subtle + that intent |
| Badge surface | `eevenkoto-badge eevenkoto-badge--solid` | solid + neutral |
| Table | `<table class="eevenkoto-table">` + bare `tr` / `th` / `td` | default variant + row stripe; cells from host descendants (kinds via `--index` / `--numeric`) |
| TableCell | `<td class="eevenkoto-table-cell">` | text kind — for cells outside a Table host |
| Prose | `<div class="eevenkoto-prose">` + bare `h*` / `p` / `ul` / `ol` / `li` | same defaults as classed type |
| Flow | Compose with Prose for bare-tag pair gaps | classed primitives always |

## CSS patterns

### Host carries default tokens and states

```css
.eevenkoto-button {
  --_eevenkoto-button-text: var(
    --eevenkoto-button-text,
    var(--eevenkoto-color-control-primary-text)
  );
  /* … full primary + md fallbacks, including elevation … */
}

/* Default interactive states on the host; exclude non-default variants */
.eevenkoto-button:hover:not(.eevenkoto-button--secondary):not(.eevenkoto-button--ghost) {
  /* primary hover publics */
}

.eevenkoto-button--primary {
  /* optional explicit alias — same publics as host defaults */
}
```

### Tag maps with `:where` (Heading)

```css
:where(h1).eevenkoto-heading,
.eevenkoto-heading--1,
.eevenkoto-prose :where(h1) {
  /* level 1 publics */
}
```

`:where` keeps tag specificity at 0 so `.eevenkoto-heading--3` wins on `h1.eevenkoto-heading.eevenkoto-heading--3`.

### Intent / variant shortcuts (Badge)

Put the **default surface** recipe on intent-only classes; higher-specificity compounds cover non-default surfaces:

```css
.eevenkoto-badge--success { /* subtle success */ }
.eevenkoto-badge--solid { /* solid neutral */ }
.eevenkoto-badge--solid.eevenkoto-badge--success { /* solid success */ }
```

## Anti-patterns

- Requiring `--primary` / `--md` / `--subtle` / `--default` for the default look
- Putting default hover only on `.eevenkoto-button--primary:hover` so host-alone buttons look dead
- Bare `h1 { … }` or `button { … }` outside Prose / host compounds
- Treating Flow as a substitute for Prose (Flow owns gaps; Prose owns bare-tag type)
## Decisions

_Source: `apps/storybook/src/foundations/decisions.mdx`_

# Decisions

Short ADRs for product scope. Component APIs live on each component’s docs page.

## Content DS, not a full app kit

Eevenkoto is a **TTRPG content design system** (statblocks, entity refs, ability scores) plus **portable core chrome** (Button, Field, Menu, table stack, typography). It is not a general application kit.

**Shipped:** Core atoms/molecules listed in package READMEs (including StatusDot, Chip, Catalog, Menu `embedded` / `status` / `locked`); Domain EntityRef (including `class` and `creature`) → AbilityScore → Statblock → Spellblock.

**Theming:** Light is the default. `[data-theme="dark"]` and `[data-surface-mode="dark"]` share the same Tier 2 remaps (Storybook toolbar). Contrast theme is not implemented.

**Token-only (no component yet):** form checkbox/radio/switch, toast/banner containers, modal surface roles, breadcrumb-as-link tokens. Do not assume a component exists because a Tier 2 token is named.

**Not in scope:** Dialog, Select, Toast, Pager, Tabs, date pickers, app shell. Popover is CSS chrome; the host app owns focus trapping and dialog behavior. Compose class pages with the [Class entry recipe](/?path=/docs/foundations-class-entry-recipe--docs) — no Classblock organism yet.

## Optional CSS peer

`@eevenkoto/html`, `@eevenkoto/react`, and `@eevenkoto/vue` list `@eevenkoto/css` as an **optional** peer so markup can be assembled without styles. Appearance requires explicit CSS imports (`styles.css` + each component sheet).

## Google Fonts

Base `styles.css` imports Inter and Outfit from Google Fonts. Consumers who cannot use that CDN should override `font-family` on `:root` / `body` or self-host.

## Print is a media restyle, not a second view

Content pages keep their screen markup. `@media print` on existing hosts (outermost [Prose](/?path=/docs/core-molecules-prose--docs), Heading, TableShell, Statblock, Spellblock, Card, Scroll, Menu) turns a long article into two snaking columns. No print-specific BEM, no `/print` route. Nested Prose sections must not open a second column context. Details: [Print columns](/?path=/docs/foundations-print-columns--docs).
## Print columns

_Source: `apps/storybook/src/foundations/print-columns.mdx`_

# Print columns

**Related:** [Prose](/?path=/docs/core-molecules-prose--docs) · [Flow](/?path=/docs/core-molecules-flow--docs) · [Decisions](/?path=/docs/foundations-decisions--docs) · [Heading](/?path=/docs/core-atoms-heading--docs)

Long-form Eevenkoto pages stay **one column on screen**. Printing the **same document** (Ctrl+P / Save as PDF) restyles outermost Prose into two snaking columns. There is no print route, no `eevenkoto-print-*` class, and no extra markup.

The live pattern is eevenko.to class pages: `article.eevenkoto-prose.eevenkoto-flow` wrapping nested `section.eevenkoto-prose.eevenkoto-flow`, bare `h1`–`h4`, TableShell, Notice, and EntityRef.

Print **this canvas** in Chrome and Firefox (the story iframe, not the Storybook manager). On screen the article must stay a single column with the lab sidebar visible.

## Architecture

Print is a restyle of existing hosts:

| Host | Print default |
| --- | --- |
| Outermost `.eevenkoto-prose` | `columns: 2`, `column-fill: auto` |
| Nested `.eevenkoto-prose` | No columns (would nest fragmentainers) |
| Direct child `h1` / `h2` of Prose | `column-span: all` (already `break-after: avoid`) |
| Statblock, Spellblock, Card, Notice | `break-inside: avoid` |
| TableShell, AbilityScoreGroup | `column-span: all` + avoid split |
| Scroll | `overflow: visible` |
| Menu, Popover, TooltipCard | `display: none` |
| `@page` (in `styles.css`) | A4, 18mm margin; `print-color-adjust: exact` on `html, body` |

Headings **inside** Statblock or Spellblock do not span: that would pull the title out of the card.

## Tall boxed organisms

One default, no author-facing print switch: **keep the box intact** (`break-inside: avoid`). If a Statblock is taller than the remaining column, the engine leaves a hole and moves the whole card. That is the handout-grade tradeoff. Do not add `--span` or `--allow-break` modifiers.

AbilityScoreGroup and class tables span both columns so a six-wide grid is not crushed to ~90mm.

## Nested Prose (required)

```css
@media print {
  .eevenkoto-prose:not(.eevenkoto-prose .eevenkoto-prose) {
    columns: 2;
  }
}
```

Applying `columns` to every Prose host would columnize each `section.doc-section` separately.

## App chrome vs DS chrome

`.layout-shell` / `.content-wrapper` belong to the site. Menu hiding stops a 139-item nav dump. Ambient glow, login, and side ribbons stay the host app’s print sheet.

## What browsers will not do

Handout-grade, not a typesetter. Fragile: last-page `column-fill: auto`, `orphans` / `widows`, `box-decoration-break: clone` on split cards. Missing: footnotes, running heads from the current heading, “see page N”. Those need a paged-media engine (Prince, WeasyPrint, Paged.js), which is out of scope.

CSS Grid cannot snake a single prose stream. Do not print the article as two independent tracks.

## Verify

1. Screen: single column; nested sections; sidebar Menu visible.
2. Chrome Print / Save as PDF: two columns, H1/H2 span, table unclipped and full width, Menu gone, EntityRefs in-flow (no tooltip cards), short Statblock unsplit.
3. Firefox Print: same checks; note last-page fill if columns look balanced instead of newspaper-filled.

**Observed (Chromium print media, A4-width canvas):** outermost Prose `column-count: 2` / `column-fill: auto`; nested section Prose stays `column-count: auto`; H1 `column-span: all`; TableShell and AbilityScoreGroup span; Scroll `overflow: visible`; Menu `display: none`; Statblock `break-inside: avoid`. Firefox Print was not run in this lab (agent browser is Chromium only).
## Class entry recipe

_Source: `apps/storybook/src/foundations/class-entry-recipe.mdx`_

# Class entry recipe

How to compose a **player class page** (Hurjapää and siblings) from shipped pieces. There is **no Classblock organism**. If this recipe is too easy to get wrong in product markup, consider a Domain organism later — do not invent Domain Heading variants.

Also read: [PropertyList](/?path=/docs/core-molecules-propertylist--docs) · [TableShell](/?path=/docs/core-organisms-tableshell--docs) · [StatblockFeature](/?path=/docs/domain-molecules-statblockfeature--docs) · [Prose](/?path=/docs/core-molecules-prose--docs) · [Spellblock](/?path=/docs/domain-organisms-spellblock--docs)

## Why to use

Class pages mix definitional stats, a level chart, and named features. Products that paint those as unlabeled paragraphs plus one-off CSS fight the Statblock/Spellblock stack. This recipe is the documented composition so eevenko.to can delete page-local class chrome.

## When to use

Use this recipe for class, background, species, or culture **entries**. Use [Spellblock](/?path=/docs/domain-organisms-spellblock--docs) for spells and [Statblock](/?path=/docs/domain-organisms-statblock--docs) for creatures. Use Catalog for indexes of those entries.

## Outline

Keep heading levels honest (H1 name → H2 sections → H3 features). Remap look on [Heading](/?path=/docs/core-atoms-heading--docs) `runIn` for feature names, not by skipping tags.

1. **Name** — page H1 (Prose / Heading). Optional [Badge](/?path=/docs/core-atoms-badge--docs) for readiness (*Valmis*) in the page header, not in the H1.
2. **Core (ydin)** — [PropertyList](/?path=/docs/core-molecules-propertylist--docs) for hit dice, proficiencies, typical abilities. Do not dump unlabeled bold-lead paragraphs.
3. **Level chart** — [Table](/?path=/docs/core-molecules-table--docs) inside [TableShell](/?path=/docs/core-organisms-tableshell--docs). Feature names in cells are [EntityRef](/?path=/docs/domain-atoms-entityref--docs) `classFeature`.
4. **Features** — one [StatblockFeature](/?path=/docs/domain-molecules-statblockfeature--docs) per named feature (run-in name + description). Subclass / manifest groups are [StatblockSection](/?path=/docs/domain-molecules-statblocksection--docs) titles (H2) wrapping features (H3).
5. Wrap the article in **Prose + Flow**.

## Do / Don’t

- Do keep locale strings as data (Finnish names in the app).
- Do use EntityRef `kind: 'class'` for the class name and `classFeature` for Hurma / Tyyli ja asenne.
- Don’t invent a Classblock until this recipe fails in real pages.
- Don’t restyle Heading in Domain CSS for “class chrome.”

## Migration (eevenko.to)

Hurjapää today: prose dumps for “Hurjapään ydin” + a table + h3 features. Replace the ydin block with PropertyList; keep TableShell; map each feature heading + following paragraphs to StatblockFeature.

# Component index

Short Why/When plus the first API table from each Storybook MDX. Full docs stay in Storybook.

### Avatar

_Source: `apps/storybook/src/core/atoms/Avatar/Avatar.mdx` · [Storybook](/?path=/docs/core-atoms-avatar-avatar--docs)_

**Why:** Rules and roster UIs need a compact face mark for a character or account without inventing ad-hoc circles. Avatar is that portrait shell — image or quiet parchment placeholder — sized on the shared sm/md/lg ladder.

**When:** Pass src when you have a portrait asset.       Omit src for the parchment user placeholder until an image exists.       Always provide name for alt / aria-label.        }   dont={            Don’t encode online status or role on the avatar — use Badge or text nearby.       Don’t invent initials or turquoise fills; the placeholder is the user icon on parchment.       Don’t use Avatar as a Button — wrap a control if the portrait is interactive.        } />

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | — | Accessible name. |
| `src` | `string` | — | Portrait URL; omit for placeholder. |
| `size` | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'` | `md` | Diameter ladder. |

### Badge

_Source: `apps/storybook/src/core/atoms/Badge/Badge.mdx` · [Storybook](/?path=/docs/core-atoms-badge-badge--docs)_

**Why:** Status and taxonomy need a compact, scannable marker beside content — readiness, severity, membership — without looking like a click target. Badge is that non-interactive chip so metadata stays visible without competing with Buttons or filters.

**When:** Status indicators with optional dot (readiness, validation state).       Non-interactive entity or role tags beside headings or rows.       Map product labels in the app (Ready, Draft) → DS intent; keep copy in the product.        }   dont={            Don’t use Badge as a clickable filter — that is Chip.       Don’t use Badge without a visible label in a nav tree — that is StatusDot.       Don’t invent local OKLCH in the component; finalize placeholder Tier 1 hues, then adjust Tier 2 mixes.       Don’t put product-specific presets (Guest, Spell) into @eevenkoto/core.       Don’t use ALL CAPS — sentence case + bold (P5).        } />

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | — | Visible text (sentence case). |
| `variant` | `'subtle' \| 'solid' \| 'outline'` | `'subtle'` | Surface recipe. |
| `intent` | `'neutral' \| 'info' \| 'success' \| 'caution' \| 'critical' \| 'admin'` | `'neutral'` | Feedback intent. |
| `size` | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'` | `'md'` | Shared size ladder. |
| `shape` | `'pill' \| 'rounded'` | `'pill'` | Corner treatment. |
| `dot` | `boolean` | `false` | Status dot (`__dot`). |

### Button

_Source: `apps/storybook/src/core/atoms/Button/Button.mdx` · [Storybook](/?path=/docs/core-atoms-button-button--docs)_

**Why:** Buttons execute actions in the interface: submitting a form, opening a dialog, cancelling an operation, or performing add/remove actions. They stand out from surrounding content and guide attention to the most important actions.

**When:** Use a Button when the user needs to perform an explicit action — initiating a task, submitting information, confirming a decision, or opening additional functionality. Prefer a Button whenever the user is expected to *do* something, not only navigate or view content.

| Arg / concern | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `'primary' \| 'secondary' \| 'ghost'` | No | `'primary'` | Maps to `eevenkoto-button--{variant}`. Host alone is also primary in CSS. |
| `label` | `string` | Yes | — | Visible text; also `aria-label` when `iconPosition` is `only`. |
| `size` | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'` | No | `'md'` | Maps to `eevenkoto-button--sm` / `--md` / `--lg`. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | No | `false` | Sets the native `disabled` attribute. |
| `icon` | `ButtonIconName` | No | — | From token `BUTTON_ICON_NAMES` (renders Icon). |
| `iconPosition` | `'left' \| 'right' \| 'only'` | No | `'left'` when icon is set | Maps to `eevenkoto-button--icon-*`. |

### Caption

_Source: `apps/storybook/src/core/atoms/Caption/Caption.mdx` · [Storybook](/?path=/docs/core-atoms-caption-caption--docs)_

**Why:** Captions keep timestamps, helper hints, and field metadata visually quieter than body copy — smaller type and tertiary ink — without inventing a one-off rem or gray.

**When:** Use Caption under form fields, on cards, or beside status metadata. Prefer Paragraph for multi-sentence prose and Heading for titles.

### Chip

_Source: `apps/storybook/src/core/atoms/Chip/Chip.mdx` · [Storybook](/?path=/docs/core-atoms-chip-chip--docs)_

**Why:** Dev role switchers and small exclusive tags need a clickable chip that is not a Badge (feedback, non-interactive) and not a full Button. Chip is that control so eevenko.to can drop `.role-chip` / `.dev-chip`.

**When:** Toggleable filters or role presets the user can select.       Use href when the chip navigates (still a Chip, not LinkButton).                Use Segmented Control when         the set is exclusive and always visible as one track (Full text ↔ SRD).               }   dont={                     Don’t use Chip for non-interactive readiness — that is{' '}         Badge or{' '}         StatusDot.              Don’t paint Chip with feedback intents; selected uses control primary.       Don’t replace a hamburger or search control with Chip — that is Button icon-only.        } />

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | — | Visible text. |
| `selected` | `boolean` | `false` | Pressed / current. |
| `size` | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'` | `'md'` | Shared control ladder. |
| `href` | `string` | — | When set, renders as `<a>`. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Non-interactive (opaque disabled tokens). |

### Frame

_Source: `apps/storybook/src/core/atoms/Frame/Frame.mdx` · [Storybook](/?path=/docs/core-atoms-frame-frame--docs)_

**Why:** Dense charts and token boards need a portable bordered panel so they read as contained rulebook surfaces instead of bleeding into the page canvas. Frame is that host — TableShell uses it by default, and other panels can reuse the same border without a one-off box.

**When:** Wrap dense charts, token panels, or any content that should read as a contained rulebook panel. Prefer bare layout when the page canvas is enough.

### Heading

_Source: `apps/storybook/src/core/atoms/Heading/Heading.mdx` · [Storybook](/?path=/docs/core-atoms-heading-heading--docs)_

**Why:** Pages need a scannable outline readers and assistive tech can trust. Heading gives six structured levels — size, weight, family, case, posture, and light rules — so titles stay consistent without faking hierarchy with bold Paragraphs or skipped levels for looks alone.

**When:** Use Heading for page titles and section labels. One `h1` per view; nest levels without skipping for style alone.

### Icon

_Source: `apps/storybook/src/core/atoms/Icon/Icon.mdx` · [Storybook](/?path=/docs/core-atoms-icon-icon--docs)_

**Why:** Chrome needs the same glyphs in Button, adornments, and product UI without each consumer pasting SVG path strings. Icon is the shared renderer (size ladder + `currentColor`); the name inventory stays in core tokens so the catalog has one source of truth.

**When:** Pick names from the Icons token         catalog — add glyphs only in tokens/icons.ts.                       Let the parent set color (currentColor). Omit label when decorative         (aria-hidden).                       Use Button’s icon prop for the four-name subset; use Icon everywhere else.               }   dont={            Don’t paste path strings into Button, Menu, or product CSS.       Don’t grow a parallel icon map next to iconPaths.                Don’t treat Icon as a click target — wrap Button or a link when the glyph is interactive.               } />

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `IconName` | — | From token `ICON_NAMES`. |
| `size` | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'` | `'md'` | Size ladder. |
| `label` | `string` | — | Accessible name; omit when decorative. |

### Inline Ref

_Source: `apps/storybook/src/core/atoms/InlineRef/InlineRef.mdx` · [Storybook](/?path=/docs/core-atoms-inlineref-inlineref--docs)_

**Why:** Body copy often points at another page, a previewable term, a name that has no page yet, or a destination the reader cannot open. InlineRef is that mark without Button chrome, Badge status, or product vocabulary — so Core Popover triggers stay Core and eevenko.to can drop `.unlinked-term` / `.tooltip-ref-locked`.

**When:** Mark an inline term that can open a Popover / TooltipCard preview.       Prefer a real href when the term has a destination URL.                Set unlinked when the term is known but has no page (italic + dotted underline,         never a link).                       Set locked when the destination is gated; keep href if login still         navigates. Override lockedLabel when the UI is localized (Lukittu).                       Use Domain EntityRef when you need         closed rules kinds (spell, condition, creature, …).               }   dont={            Don’t invent Domain kinds on InlineRef — that is EntityRef.       Don’t use InlineRef for status or readiness — that is Badge.       Don’t wrap InlineRef in a Button; the link (or tag) is the trigger.       Don’t embed Lucide (or other) lock SVGs — use locked and the Icon token.                Don’t set both unlinked and href expecting a link; unlinked always         renders a span.               } />

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | — | Visible label. |
| `href` | `string` | — | When set (and not `unlinked`), renders as `<a>`. |
| `unlinked` | `boolean` | `false` | Known term, no destination (`span` + `--unlinked`). |
| `locked` | `boolean` | `false` | Trailing lock Icon + visually hidden `lockedLabel`. |
| `lockedLabel` | `string` | `'Locked'` | Accessible lock name; override when localized. |

### Input

_Source: `apps/storybook/src/core/atoms/Input/Input.mdx` · [Storybook](/?path=/docs/core-atoms-input-input--docs)_

**Why:** Every product form should not invent its own text-box surface. Input owns fill, border, focus, and invalid chrome once; Field (or equivalent host markup) owns the labeling contract around it.

**When:** Nest Input inside Field for forms; pass matching id /{' '}         describedBy / invalid from the Field message.                       Use ariaLabel only when there is genuinely no visible label (chrome search).                       Treat placeholder as an example value — never as the accessible name.               }   dont={                     Don’t treat Input as a complete form field (no visible label + no Field).                       Don’t pass a visible-label string as Input ariaLabel when Field already has{' '}         label — that duplicates the name.                       Don’t show invalid chrome without Field error text linked via{' '}         describedBy.               } />

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `string` | — | Wire to Field `htmlFor` / `<label for>`. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | — | `aria-label` when **no** visible Field label. |
| `describedBy` | `string` | — | `aria-describedby` (Field message id). |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | `false` | Invalid paint + `aria-invalid`. |
| `placeholder` | `string` | — | Example hint, not the name. |
| `search` | `boolean` | `false` | Pill + search icon recipe. |

### LinkButton

_Source: `apps/storybook/src/core/atoms/LinkButton/LinkButton.mdx` · [Storybook](/?path=/docs/core-atoms-linkbutton-linkbutton--docs)_

**Why:** Call-to-action navigation needs a control that *looks* like a button so it can compete with surrounding chrome, but it must remain a link: it has a destination, can be opened in a new tab, and participates in the browser’s link model. Putting `href` on Button (or wrapping Button in an anchor) mixes those roles.

**When:** Use a LinkButton when the user should **go somewhere** and that destination is a primary or secondary marketing action (hero, empty state, campaign banner). Use [Button](/?path=/docs/core-atoms-button--docs) when the user **does** something on the page. Use [InlineRef](/?path=/docs/core-atoms-inlineref--docs) for terms inside running text.

| Arg / concern | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `href` | `string` | Yes | — | Destination URL. |
| `variant` | `'primary' \| 'secondary'` | No | `'primary'` | Maps to `eevenkoto-link-button--{variant}`. Host alone is also primary. |
| `label` | `string` | Yes | — | Visible chrome copy. |
| `size` | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'` | No | `'md'` | Maps to `--sm` / `--md` / `--lg`. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | No | `false` | Removes `href`; adds `aria-disabled` + `tabindex="-1"`. Prefer omitting. |
| `icon` | `ButtonIconName` | No | — | From `BUTTON_ICON_NAMES`. |
| `iconPosition` | `'left' \| 'right'` | No | `'right'` when icon is set | Maps to `--icon-*`. |
| `target` | `string` | No | — | Native `target`. |
| `rel` | `string` | No | — | Native `rel`; `_blank` automatically adds `noopener noreferrer`. |

### Paragraph

_Source: `apps/storybook/src/core/atoms/Paragraph/Paragraph.mdx` · [Storybook](/?path=/docs/core-atoms-paragraph-paragraph--docs)_

**Why:** Consistent body type keeps reading rhythm stable across pages and themes. Semantic sizes let density or theme remaps change roles without renaming the rem ladder.

**When:** Use Paragraph for multi-sentence body copy. Prefer Heading for titles and Caption for short metadata.

### Popover

_Source: `apps/storybook/src/core/atoms/Popover/Popover.mdx` · [Storybook](/?path=/docs/core-atoms-popover-popover--docs)_

**Why:** Short-lived secondary content — entity previews, compact help, a small menu shell — needs an elevated surface next to a trigger without the weight of a dialog. Popover is that chrome; the app still owns show/hide, focus, and collision.

**When:** Use the panel as chrome and let the app own show/hide, delays, Escape, and         collision.                       Anchor preview tooltips on InlineRef links (Core). Use Domain{' '}         EntityRef when closed kinds are         required.                       Nest TooltipCard for header /         body / footer inside the panel.                       Prefer fixed + portal to body when the trigger lives in scrolling         or overflowing prose.               }   dont={                     Don’t assume a Button trigger — Storybook demos once used buttons for convenience only.                       Don’t put Floating UI / Popper inside @eevenkoto/css. Positioning math stays in         the app (or a future optional helper package).                       Don’t use Popover for blocking multi-step flows — that is a dialog pattern with focus         management you own carefully.                       Don’t double chrome: either plain content in Popover, or TooltipCard nested (it sheds its         own border/shadow as a direct child).               } />

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `placement` | `'top' \| 'bottom' \| 'left' \| 'right'` | `'bottom'` | Absolute placement. Ignored when `fixed`. |
| `arrow` | `boolean` | `false` | Renders `__arrow`. |
| `fixed` | `boolean` | `false` | Portal / JS-positioned overlay. |
| `open` | `boolean` | `false` | Visible state for `fixed` panels. |
| `label` | `string` | — | `aria-label` on the panel. |
| `content` | `string` | — | HTML package: panel inner HTML. |
| `role` | `'dialog' \| 'tooltip' \| 'note' \| 'group'` | — | Optional ARIA role. |

### Property

_Source: `apps/storybook/src/core/atoms/Property/Property.mdx` · [Storybook](/?path=/docs/core-atoms-property-property--docs)_

**Why:** Pair a definition term with its value without inventing a new layout. The atom keeps `dt`/`dd` semantics so assistive tech reads the association.

**When:** Use Property inside a `dl` (PropertyList) for keyed facts. Do not use it for running prose or for interactive form fields (use Field).

### Scroll

_Source: `apps/storybook/src/core/atoms/Scroll/Scroll.mdx` · [Storybook](/?path=/docs/core-atoms-scroll-scroll--docs)_

**Why:** Wide tables and tall panels overflow the frame. Scroll owns the overflow axis (and sticky cues when composed) so hosts like TableShell do not invent one-off `overflow` CSS per layout.

**When:** Wrap content that may exceed the viewport or frame. TableShell enables Scroll by default around Table.

### Card

_Source: `apps/storybook/src/core/molecules/Card/Card.mdx` · [Storybook](/?path=/docs/core-molecules-card-card--docs)_

**Why:** Item entries, paywall summaries, and other self-contained chunks need a surface with optional title and footer chrome — not a full page layout and not a bare Frame. Card owns that sectioned box so products do not invent one-off bordered panels for every teaser. Copy-paste HTML is a document (`article` + heading), not a div sandwich.

**When:** Author real &lt;article&gt; / &lt;header&gt; /{' '}         &lt;h2&gt; / &lt;p&gt; / &lt;footer&gt; (or pass{' '}         title / body / footer to renderCard).              Group related content that reads as one unit (item card, gate summary, teaser).       Omit unused sections — body-only is still a valid Card.                Use elevated when the card should float above the page (overlays, pinned         summaries). Don’t swap the host to &lt;a&gt; — inner header /{' '}         footer would belong to the page, not the card.                       Don’t mark a Card interactive without a real href (or button) — hover alone is         not enough.              Don’t bake product layout or paywall copy into the Card API — keep strings as data.        } />

### Field

_Source: `apps/storybook/src/core/molecules/Field/Field.mdx` · [Storybook](/?path=/docs/core-molecules-field-field--docs)_

**Why:** Form controls fail WCAG when the name is only a placeholder, or when invalid state is red chrome with no words. Field owns the visible label and the hint/error message so that contract stays consistent — Input stays control chrome, not a half-built form row.

**When:** Always show a visible label for form data entry.                When invalid, set error on Field and invalid +{' '}         describedBy on Input (same message id).                       Use hint for helper text; it yields to error when both would         apply.              Keep placeholder as an example value only.        }   dont={            Don’t mark a field invalid with red chrome and no error string.       Don’t use placeholder (or aria-label alone) instead of a visible label in forms.                Don’t omit htmlFor / matching Input id — the label must         associate.               } />

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | — | Visible label. |
| `htmlFor` | `string` | slug from label (HTML) | Control id. |
| `hint` | `string` | — | Helper text when no error. |
| `error` | `string` | — | Error text (takes priority over hint). |
| `messageId` | `string` | `` `${htmlFor}-message` `` | Id for `aria-describedby`. |
| `control` | `string` | — | HTML package: nested control markup. |

### Flow

_Source: `apps/storybook/src/core/molecules/Flow/Flow.mdx` · [Storybook](/?path=/docs/core-molecules-flow-flow--docs)_

**Why:** Type primitives need default margins for standalone stories, but those margins **stack** in compositions — especially with global `text-box` trim removing half-leading. Flow owns the gaps instead.

**When:** Wrap any vertical stack of Heading / Paragraph / Caption / List (and nested Flows) in `eevenkoto-flow`. For bare CMS/`h*`/`p`/`ul`/`ol` markup, compose with [Prose](/?path=/docs/core-molecules-prose--docs) (`eevenkoto-prose eevenkoto-flow`).

### List

_Source: `apps/storybook/src/core/molecules/List/List.mdx` · [Storybook](/?path=/docs/core-molecules-list-list--docs)_

**Why:** Reading content often needs bulleted or numbered steps. Real `ul` / `ol` / `li` keep semantics honest for assistive tech and let Prose style bare CMS tags the same way as classed Lists.

**When:** Use List for unordered or ordered content lists in reading layouts. Prefer PropertyList for vitals and other definitional metadata. Prefer Paragraph for multi-sentence prose without markers.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `ListItemProps[]` | — | Rows to render. |
| `variant` | `'unordered' \| 'ordered'` | `unordered` | List kind / element. |
| `size` | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'` | `md` | Body type size. |
| `tone` | `'primary' \| 'secondary'` | `primary` | Content color. |
| `text` (item) | `string` | — | Item copy. |

### Menu

_Source: `apps/storybook/src/core/molecules/Menu/Menu.mdx` · [Storybook](/?path=/docs/core-molecules-menu-menu--docs)_

**Why:** Account menus, view switchers, and worldbook sidebars all need a compact vertical list of destinations. Menu owns that chrome — flat rows for Popover menus, nested `group` branches for eevenko.to-style trees — without baking open/position or routing into the DS. Copy-paste HTML navigates with no app JS.

**When:** Author real &lt;a href&gt; rows (or pass href to{' '}         renderMenu) so the menu works as a document.                       Use flat items (+ header/separator) for account and action menus inside{' '}         Popover. Prefer links to profile,         billing, and sign-out URLs.                       Use nested kind: 'group' for multi-level nav (section → subsection → leaf         links), as on eevenko.to. Hand HTML is &lt;li&gt;&lt;details&gt; with a nested{' '}         &lt;ul&gt;.                       Put an overview page as the first child link when a section has both an index and children         (e.g. “Lajit” link under the Lajit branch).                       Set expanded on a group (or the open attribute on{' '}         details) when that branch should start open (current section).                       Set embedded when the menu sits in a sunken sidebar (transparent, no raised         panel). Leave the default raised host for Popover menus.                       Pass status + statusLabel for a trailing{' '}         StatusDot; locked for a         lock Icon. Labels truncate with ellipsis.               }   dont={                     Don’t default to inert &lt;button&gt; rows in HTML. Buttons are an escape hatch         for in-page commands with no URL.              Don’t fake nesting with only header + visual indent — use group / details.       Don’t put role=&quot;menu&quot; + arrow-key behavior on the host unless the app also implements that contract (host is &lt;nav&gt;).       Don’t wrap Menu in a second &lt;nav&gt; — the host is already the landmark.       Don’t use Menu for page body outlines — that is Heading + Flow / Prose.        } />

| Entry `kind` | Fields |
| --- | --- |
| `item` (default) | `id`, `label`, `href?`, `selected?`, `disabled?`, `locked?`, `lockedLabel?`, `status?`, `statusLabel?` |
| `header` | `label` |
| `separator` | — |
| `group` | `id`, `label`, `expanded?`, `children: MenuEntry[]` |

### Notice

### Prose

_Source: `apps/storybook/src/core/molecules/Prose/Prose.mdx` · [Storybook](/?path=/docs/core-molecules-prose-prose--docs)_

**Why:** CMS HTML, markdown, and editorial content often ship tags without DS classes. Prose opts those tags into the type system without restyling every `h1`/`p`/`ul` in the document.

**When:** Wrap reading/CMS content in eevenkoto-prose — bare ul/ol match List.       Compose eevenkoto-prose eevenkoto-flow when you need pair-aware gaps. ### Segmented Control

_Source: `apps/storybook/src/core/molecules/SegmentedControl/SegmentedControl.mdx` · [Storybook](/?path=/docs/core-molecules-segmentedcontrol-segmentedcontrol--docs)_

**Why:** Mutually exclusive short options often need to stay visible as a compact track — not hidden in a select or scattered as separate Buttons. Segmented Control is that exclusive-choice chrome for in-page radios or navigational link sets.

**When:** Radios for an in-page setting that stays on this document.                       Links when each option is a different URL (Full text vs Short SRD). ### Tooltip Card

_Source: `apps/storybook/src/core/molecules/TooltipCard/TooltipCard.mdx` · [Storybook](/?path=/docs/core-molecules-tooltipcard-tooltipcard--docs)_

Don’t ship tooltip show/hide JS in the DS — that stays in the app.        } />

### TableShell

_Source: `apps/storybook/src/core/organisms/TableShell/TableShell.mdx` · [Storybook](/?path=/docs/core-organisms-tableshell-tableshell--docs)_

### Entity Ref

_Source: `apps/storybook/src/domain/atoms/EntityRef/EntityRef.mdx` · [Storybook](/?path=/docs/domain-atoms-entityref-entityref--docs)_

**Why:** Rules prose names other entities constantly. EntityRef marks those names with **kind-colored** ink so readers can tell a referenced term from ordinary words — without Badge chrome or a Button. Prefer bare [InlineRef](/?path=/docs/core-atoms-inlineref--docs) when you do not need a closed kind.

**When:** Point at another rules entity inside body copy (Frightened, Advantage,{' '}         Cure Wounds) when a kind color matters.                       Prefer a real href when the entity has a page — tooltips and deep links hang off         that link.                       Keep the visible string as the entity name; localize the name in app data,         not in the kind API.                       Use the closed kind set so ink and hover chip map to the right Tier 2 tuple.                       Use kind: &apos;class&apos; for class names (Hurjapää, mystikko) and{' '}         classFeature for features (Hurma). Use creature for         opponents (Haukka). Map gear (tikari, varuste/esine) to item         — do not add a Finnish kind.                       Pass locked / unlinked from Core InlineRef instead of product lock         SVGs or .unlinked-term.               }   dont={                     Don’t use EntityRef for a generic Core preview trigger — that is{' '}         InlineRef.                       Don’t use EntityRef for status or readiness — that is{' '}         Badge.                       Don’t invent open-ended kinds in props. New kinds are a design decision (CSS +{' '}         EntityRefKind), not a free string. Don’t add varuste — that is{' '}         item.                       Don’t keep a .tooltip-ref class that reassigns InlineRef bridges from{' '}         data-ref-tyyppi.                       Don’t wrap EntityRef in a Button. The trigger for entity tooltips is the link itself.                       Don’t rely on a permanent filled chip in dense prose — rest state is ink + underline only.               } />

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | — | Visible entity name. |
| `kind` | `EntityRefKind` | `'item'` | Closed kind set. |
| `href` | `string` | — | When set (and not `unlinked`), renders as `<a>`. |
| `unlinked` | `boolean` | `false` | Inherited from InlineRef. |
| `locked` | `boolean` | `false` | Inherited from InlineRef. |
| `lockedLabel` | `string` | `'Locked'` | Inherited from InlineRef. |

### AbilityScore

_Source: `apps/storybook/src/domain/molecules/AbilityScore/AbilityScore.mdx` · [Storybook](/?path=/docs/domain-molecules-abilityscore-abilityscore--docs)_

**Why:** Ability columns are decorative and positional (orbiting chips), but still need accessible terms for score / modifier / save. AbilityScore owns that column AT contract.

**When:** Pass ability names as data (Karisma, Ketteryys) — never as core enums.       Override scoreLabel / modifierLabel / saveLabel / proficientLabel for Finnish (Arvo, Muuttuja, Pelastus, pätevä).       Set saveProficient when the creature is proficient — bright shield border only.        }   dont={            Don’t use Badge for these numbers — Badge is feedback; Stat is content display.       Don’t use bright gold on every chip — reserve content-accent-strong for proficient saves.       Don’t style adjacent paragraphs into a sandwich — compose [AbilityScoreGroup](/?path=/docs/domain-organisms-abilityscoregroup--docs).        } />

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | — | Ability name (column header). |
| `labelId` | `string` | derived | Optional stable id for `aria-labelledby`. |
| `score` | `string` | — | Base score. |
| `modifier` | `string` | — | Modifier (typically signed). |
| `save` | `string` | — | Save bonus (typically signed). |
| `scoreLabel` | `string` | `'Score'` | Visually hidden term. |
| `modifierLabel` | `string` | `'Modifier'` | Visually hidden term. |
| `saveLabel` | `string` | `'Save'` | Visually hidden term. |
| `saveProficient` | `boolean` | `false` | Emphasized shield + proficient suffix in the hidden term. |
| `proficientLabel` | `string` | `'proficient'` | Suffix inside the hidden save term when proficient. |

### StatblockFeature

_Source: `apps/storybook/src/domain/molecules/StatblockFeature/StatblockFeature.mdx` · [Storybook](/?path=/docs/domain-molecules-statblockfeature-statblockfeature--docs)_

**Why:** Feature names should participate in the document outline without orphaning a full-width heading above a one-line mechanic. Run-in H3 keeps the name on the same line as the body while remaining a real heading.

**When:** Attacks, traits, bonus actions, reactions, legendary actions.       Nest under StatblockSection (or any H2 cluster).       Pass the name without a trailing period — CSS appends .  via ::after.        }   dont={            Don’t fake the name with &lt;strong&gt;&lt;em&gt; inside a Paragraph.       Don’t use H6 for features inside a Statblock — that skips levels; use the run-in at the level the outline needs.       Don’t put the colon or period in the name string.        } />

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | — | Feature title (run-in heading). |
| `level` | `2 \| 3 \| 6` | `3` | Semantic heading level for `name`. Appearance is identical at every level. |
| `description` | `string` (HTML) / `ReactNode` (React) | — | Body after the run-in. |

### StatblockSection

_Source: `apps/storybook/src/domain/molecules/StatblockSection/StatblockSection.mdx` · [Storybook](/?path=/docs/domain-molecules-statblocksection-statblocksection--docs)_

**Why:** Grouping features under a real H2 keeps the outline contiguous under the creature H1 and gives a clear landmark for Actions, Reactions, Legendary Actions, and similar clusters.

**When:** Actions, bonus actions, reactions, legendary / lair actions, traits clusters.       Reuse outside a full Statblock when a rules page only needs one section.       Pass product copy for title (Toiminnot, Reaktiot) — no DS enums.        }   dont={            Don’t use H3 or H5 for the section title inside a Statblock — that breaks H1 → H2 → H3.       Don’t put feature bodies directly under the H2 without StatblockFeature (loses run-in + remap).       Don’t invent a second visual heading scale; remap happens here via Tier 3 bridges.        } />

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `string` | — | Section heading (H2). |
| `features` | `StatblockFeatureProps[]` | — | Stacked feature entries. |

**Why:** Ability grids need a panel, noise surface, scoop corners, and a container query. AbilityScore owns one column; AbilityScoreGroup owns the sandwich layout.

### Spellblock

_Source: `apps/storybook/src/domain/organisms/Spellblock/Spellblock.mdx` · [Storybook](/?path=/docs/domain-organisms-spellblock-spellblock--docs)_

**Why:** Spell pages need the same structure a printed spell has: find the school line, then Range and Duration, then read the effect. Spellblock gives you one organism that:

**When:** Spell entries on rules pages, and spell catalogs via deck.       Keep level, school, ritual tags, and component copy in the product — map them into props.       Put the whole level/school string in typeLine, exactly as it is printed.        }   dont={            Don’t rebuild the legacy &lt;strong&gt;Kantama:&lt;/strong&gt; + &lt;br&gt; paragraph block.       Don’t add school / ritual / concentration enums to @eevenkoto/core — they are strings.       Don’t use Spellblock for creatures — that is Statblock.       Don’t nest a Spellblock inside a Core Card; the organism already owns its surface.        } />

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | — | Spell name. |
| `nameLevel` | `1 \| 2` | `1` | Heading level for the name (use `2` in embeds). |
| `typeLine` | `string` | — | Italic level / school line on the plate. |
| `classes` | `PropertyItem[]` | — | Optional catalog rail under the type line. |
| `properties` | `PropertyItem[]` | — | Casting time, range, components, duration. |
| `paragraphs` | `string[]` | — | Effect prose, one entry per paragraph. |
| `features` | `StatblockFeatureProps[]` | — | Scaling run-ins. The level is derived from `nameLevel`; do not set it per item. |
| `deck` | `boolean` | `false` | Compact card for grids. |
| `lang` | `string` | — | BCP 47 tag on the article; enables `hyphens: auto`. |

### Statblock

_Source: `apps/storybook/src/domain/organisms/Statblock/Statblock.mdx` · [Storybook](/?path=/docs/domain-organisms-statblock-statblock--docs)_

**Why:** Rules pages need a stable, accessible structure for NPC and monster entries. Statblock gives you one organism that:

**When:** Full NPC, monster, or archetype entries in rules docs.       Keep ability names, vitals labels, and feature copy in the product — map them into props.       Compose from smaller molecules when you only need a grid, a section, or a single feature.        }   dont={            Don’t revive the Markdown &lt;table class="kykylistaus-table"&gt; + sibling-paragraph sandwich.       Don’t put Finnish ability enums or CR math into @eevenkoto/core.       Don’t skip heading levels for style (e.g. H1 → H6) — use H2 / H3 run-in; visuals remap on the molecules.       Don’t use Statblock for generic page chrome — it is an entry organism, not a Card.        } />

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | — | Creature / entity title. |
| `nameLevel` | `1 \| 2` | `1` | Heading level for the name (use `2` in embeds). |
| `flavor` | `string` | — | Optional flavor Paragraph. |
| `typeLine` | `string` | — | Optional italic type line. |
| `vitals` | `PropertyItem[]` | — | Combat vitals → AbilityScoreGroup header. |
| `abilities` | `AbilityScoreProps[]` | — | Ability columns. |
| `details` | `PropertyItem[]` | — | Skills / senses / languages / CR → footer. |
| `sections` | `StatblockSectionProps[]` | — | Actions, reactions, etc. |
